sections.heading: 2. Configure twelve layers without twelve expensive platforms
paragraphs: Build the stack around one customer record, one commercial approval trail, and one accounting ledger. The twelve-layer matrix gives exact planning price points and named tiers, not a claim that checkout prices were verified today. Prices are USD list-price assumptions before taxes, discounts, and optional features; annual commitments can require cash earlier than monthly accounting expense suggests. Recheck the vendor's current offer before purchase. For two users, Google Workspace Business Starter at $7 per user monthly on an annual commitment contributes $14, Bitwarden Teams at $4 contributes $8, one DocuSign Personal seat contributes $10, and one Backblaze Computer Backup subscription contributes $9. That $41 monthly-equivalent software subtotal covers only the stated quantities; it excludes hardware, additional endpoints, professional services, insurance, labor, and usage charges. The free layers do not make the whole business free to operate. Start Microsoft CSP through an authorized indirect provider rather than assuming a new company satisfies direct-bill requirements. For AWS CPPO, confirm seller eligibility, the independent software vendor's selling authorization, and the supported commercial arrangement. A zero-dollar account subscription says nothing about transaction charges or responsibility for supplier payment. Document those charges separately in each deal worksheet.

Configure identity before importing customer contacts or vendor credentials. Use individual accounts, phishing-resistant multifactor authentication where supported, two controlled recovery administrators, and an offline recovery record. A password manager stores secrets; it does not replace account-level permissions or employee offboarding. Google Workspace Business Starter is a narrow entry tier, so do not assume advanced retention, endpoint controls, or audit capabilities that belong to other editions. BitLocker requires a supporting Windows edition; FileVault is available on supported Macs. Record endpoint encryption status, patch ownership, and recovery-key custody. Backblaze Computer Backup protects selected endpoint data, not every SaaS record or cloud mailbox. Export the CRM, accounting records, signed agreements, and license ledger on a defined schedule, then restore a sample into an isolated workspace. Cloudflare DNS and a UptimeRobot HTTP check establish basic reachability signals, not customer application monitoring. GitHub Free can version quote templates and operating scripts, but credentials and customer records stay outside repositories. Where a customer requires single sign-on, longer audit retention, regional hosting, or a signed data-processing agreement, price the necessary tier into the contract before accepting the requirement. A low subscription price is useful only when its actual controls match the workload.

Connect the layers with a deliberately small data model: customer identifier, legal purchasing entity, vendor identifier, registration reference, offer identifier, subscription identifier, invoice identifier, renewal date, and collection status. Keep offer expiration separate from subscription renewal. HubSpot Free tracks opportunities; an access-controlled Google Sheet can hold the initial entitlement ledger; Wave Starter records invoices and expenses where its geography and feature set fit the business. Do not pretend a spreadsheet provides transactional locking or a full audit trail. Once simultaneous editing creates reconciliation errors, migrate the ledger to a database with permissions and change history. Trigger renewal reminders at ninety, sixty, and thirty days, then require a human review before issuing binding prices. Quote automation should populate quantities and approved price schedules without inventing discount authority. License reconciliation should compare purchased quantities, delivered entitlements, and active assignments, flagging differences rather than automatically deleting access. Avoid a paid integration platform until repeated manual work has a measurable cost. If a connector costs $50 monthly and saves two hours valued at $40 each, its illustrative benefit is $30 before maintenance; one broken mapping can reverse that result. Retain a manual export-and-reconcile procedure for every automation.

sections.heading: 3. Establish entity, payment, insurance, and contract evidence
paragraphs: Form the selling entity in a jurisdiction justified by actual operations, obtain its employer identification number directly through the IRS, and open business banking under the same legal name used in customer and vendor contracts. State filing charges vary, while the IRS does not charge for an EIN. Confirm foreign qualification and state tax registrations where required by activities and nexus; software and implementation tax treatment varies by jurisdiction and delivery method. Collect exemption certificates before applying an exemption rather than improvising after an audit request. Maintain separate operating, tax, and reserve ledger balances even if the bank uses subaccounts. The $250,000 standard FDIC insurance amount is per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category, not per account label. Review coverage if balances grow or a platform distributes funds among banks. Verify bank instructions through a previously established contact before changing supplier payment details; an emailed replacement invoice is insufficient. Assign one person to prepare payments and another to review new beneficiaries and unusual amounts. At a two-person company, that separation is practical and substantially cheaper than recovering a misdirected annual license payment. Store tax records and bank evidence outside the salesperson's personal mailbox.

Buy insurance against the work actually promised. Technology errors and omissions coverage should reflect failed implementation, configuration mistakes, and contractual service allegations; cyber coverage should address the company's own incident costs and relevant third-party exposures. Ask the broker to identify exclusions affecting contractual liability, funds-transfer fraud, subcontractors, and work outside declared territories. Compare deductible, aggregate limit, retroactive date, notification duties, and subcontractor requirements, not just premium. A certificate alone does not establish that a particular loss is covered. Make the master agreement, statement of work, purchase order, and vendor license terms agree on scope, payment, cancellation, support boundaries, and acceptance evidence. State who can authorize changes and which party is responsible for migrations, backups, customer identity access, and third-party outages. Federal commercial computer software procurement raises specific license questions under FAR 12.212; a commercial reseller cannot assume every standard vendor term becomes enforceable merely because a buyer signs an order. Confirm the customer's purchasing authority and procurement path before provisioning. E-SIGN supports electronic records and signatures under 15 U.S.C. 7001, but the operational requirement remains preserving the executed record and proving who accepted which version.

Treat regulated customer data as a separate architectural decision, not an incidental CRM attachment. A reseller that receives protected health information while performing covered functions may become a business associate; map the actual role before collecting patient-level records. Where applicable, 45 CFR 164.502(e) and 164.504(e) govern business associate arrangements, while the Security Rule requires applicable administrative, physical, and technical safeguards. The inexpensive baseline stack is not designated as a patient-data environment. Use synthetic records during demonstrations and restrict normal sales systems to commercial contacts, contract identifiers, and aggregated workload estimates. If delivery requires sensitive records, procure supported services, execute the necessary agreements, implement access and retention controls, and price that operating burden before accepting the work. Apply the same discipline to customer administrator access: grant the minimum role, time-limit delegated permissions where supported, and capture the customer authorization. A Microsoft CSP relationship does not justify unrestricted tenant administration, and an AWS marketplace purchase does not itself authorize entering the customer's account. Close the loop at offboarding by removing delegated access, transferring documentation, returning or deleting data according to the agreement, and retaining only the transaction evidence that the documented retention schedule requires.

sections.heading: 4. Prove nine mapped plays before expanding commitments
paragraphs: Use nine mapped plays as distinct worksheets, not nine businesses launched simultaneously. Only the specialty-drug identifier is supplied as a formal play identifier; the other eight names below are chapter-local channel execution patterns. Authorized AWS CPPO spread, Microsoft CSP seat resale, and registered enterprise license resale all begin with written authority and an accurate supplier purchase price. Implementation spreads then depend on a bounded scope and measured contractor hours. Renewal recovery, license reconciliation services, prepaid onboarding, and procurement evidence services monetize specific operating work without claiming customer savings as reseller revenue. Each worksheet separates customer billings, direct costs, contribution, collection timing, and allocated overhead. For example, a $12,000 implementation using eighty contractor hours at $75 costs $6,000 and contributes $6,000 before overhead; twenty additional hours reduce that contribution to $4,500. Use explicit acceptance milestones and change orders rather than assuming automation eliminates overruns. None of the illustrative play contributions changes the canonical annual profit cases, and the nine examples are not additive forecasts. The same customer could buy several services, creating duplicate counting unless each invoice line and underlying obligation has a unique reference. Choose one resale rail and one adjacent service first, then expand only after reconciliation and collections work repeatedly.

The supplied erisa_self_funded_specialty_drug_importation_arbitrage play describes self-funded employers with 100–5,000 employees, specialty biologics and GLP-1 products priced at $6,000–$15,000 monthly in the United States, and proposed overseas sourcing at $800–$2,200. Those figures are supplied commercial hypotheses, not verified prices, evidence of identical approved products, or proof of permitted importation. At $8,000 versus $1,500 monthly, the arithmetic difference is $78,000 annually; a 30% fee would be $23,400, leaving $54,600 before dispensing, logistics, clinical, and administrative costs. The broader supplied fee range of 25–35% against $50,000–$100,000 savings implies $12,500–$35,000, but savings must use actual net employer costs rather than PBM list prices. ERISA status does not create a federal drug-importation exemption: 29 U.S.C. 1144(d) preserves other federal law. The importation framework in 21 U.S.C. 384 excludes biological products and other specified categories, and foreign pharmacy licensure alone does not establish a lawful United States supply route. Do not fund purchasing or promise zero copays on that premise. The practical fallback is domestic bridge-fill coordination and manufacturer patient assistance screening through qualified providers, working with independent TPAs and transparent pass-through PBMs while respecting program eligibility and applicable benefit rules.

Keep that healthcare adjacency outside the software reseller's startup inventory and canonical revenue forecast. A lawful opportunity for this chapter is selling workflow software, implementation, or documented administrative services to an appropriately authorized operator, not acting as a pharmacy because a spreadsheet shows an attractive spread. If a $10,000 workflow implementation requires $6,000 of direct delivery, the reseller's contribution is $4,000 before overhead; employer drug spending and patient savings remain outside its revenue. Before launch, execute a complete synthetic transaction from opportunity through signed offer, supplier order, entitlement delivery, customer invoice, payment reconciliation, and renewal reminder. Introduce one deliberate failure at each boundary: expired authorization, incorrect tenant identifier, delayed settlement, and rejected acceptance. Confirm that the process stops the commitment and assigns a responsible person rather than merely sending an ignored notification. Require current authorization, adequate stressed liquidity, demonstrated delivery controls, and complete contract evidence before taking a binding order. After the first five deals, review realized contribution and collection days against the worksheet. Increase subscription tiers or contractor capacity only when measured workload justifies the change. The $150,000 capitalization supports more resilience, not permission to accumulate unused applications or extend unpriced customer credit.

callout.title: Four proofs required before the first binding order
callout.body: A successful demonstration is insufficient. The accountable operator must retain evidence that the commercial and delivery chain can perform.
items: Authorization: confirm reseller status, permitted territory, current registration, applicable license terms, and authority to issue the specific offer.
Liquidity: stress collections by thirty days, include all committed supplier payments, and preserve the documented minimum reserve after the proposed order.

Its annual owner-profit cases are $24,000 Conservative, $196,000 Base, and $500,000 Scaled. The actual killers are uncapped purchase commitments, reversible incentives, unpriced service work, and permissions that fail under audit. Build a transaction-level evidence ledger, reserve disputed economics, and stop incremental exposure before attractive bookings become cash losses.

sections.heading: 1. Break the Nine Plays into Verifiable Rights and Reversible Economics
paragraphs: Start with the permission chain, not the discount sheet. Authorized VAR resale fails when an enthusiastic salesperson mistakes distributor access for permission to sell every vendor, geography, customer class, and subscription edition. AWS Channel Partner Private Offers, or CPPO, require the relevant selling authorization and offer configuration; an attractive wholesale price does not establish customer eligibility or control settlement timing. Microsoft Cloud Solution Provider, or CSP, requires the correct partner relationship, customer agreement, and subscription commitments. For each quote, archive the applicable program terms, authorization identifier, customer legal entity, tenant or account identifier, currency, term, cancellation rights, and distributor purchase conditions. A $100,000 sale against an $88,000 supplier commitment appears to create $12,000 before other costs, but a rejected customer purchase can leave the entire $88,000 payable. These are illustrative transaction figures, not alternative scorecard cases. The fallback is a nonbinding estimate until eligibility and acceptance evidence exist, followed by a customer commitment aligned with the supplier obligation. If the vendor will not permit the intended route, sell separately scoped implementation work rather than routing the license through another customer's account. Keep the evidence attached to the transaction, not buried in a salesperson's inbox.

The next traps are expired deal registration, duplicate opportunities, conditional rebates, and private offers priced against the wrong settlement basis. Deal-registration protection is a contractual benefit with conditions; it is not ownership of the customer. Record registration expiry and whether renewals, affiliates, expansion seats, or competing partners receive different treatment. Suppose a $120,000 order costs $108,000 before an expected $6,000 incentive. The transaction has $12,000 of initial spread, not $18,000 of secure contribution. Missing proof of customer acceptance can erase the incentive after commissions have already been paid. Treat incentive eligibility, submission, acceptance, settlement, and possible recovery as separate ledger states. AWS and distributor fees vary by route and agreement; never copy a percentage from a different seller's screenshot. For Microsoft subscriptions, verify the current cancellation and seat reduction windows for the actual product and commitment rather than promising monthly exit because billing occurs monthly. Freeze the specific SKU quote when the rights evidence expires. A valid fallback is a revised price without the incentive, a shorter commitment where available, or customer-funded prepaid exposure. A competitor's willingness to promise unsupported terms is evidence of risk, not a pricing benchmark.

Implementation spreads, managed renewals, license reconciliation, and procurement enablement complete the ordinary commercial workstreams; the ninth play, the supplied 340B workflow, receives separate treatment below. Each needs independent acceptance criteria. A $30,000 implementation budgeted at 120 contractor hours costing $100 each leaves $18,000 before internal labor and overhead. An additional 100 unpaid hours remove $10,000 immediately. Require a statement of work that defines migration volume, integrations, identity configuration, test cases, and the customer dependencies that pause the schedule. Managed renewals need written renewal authority, not an assumption that last year's purchase order repeats. License reconciliation needs permitted administrative access and exportable entitlement evidence, not shared global credentials. Procurement enablement must distinguish purchasing assistance from representing that the reseller holds a government schedule or manufacturer certification. Selling evaluation keys, misstating end customers, duplicating rebate claims, inventing certifications, or creating replacement accounts after suspension can produce termination, recovery demands, intellectual-property claims, and permanent exclusion under applicable program terms. Preserve logs and use the documented appeal process instead. The circuit-breaker is simple: when a promised right cannot be demonstrated, stop that promise while continuing separately authorized support and data-return obligations.

sections.heading: 2. Reconcile Gross Billings to Owner Profit and Cash at Risk
paragraphs: Use the canonical scorecard without silently switching revenue definitions. Conservative is $300,000 of gross license resale and service billings at 8% net margin, yielding $24,000 annual owner net profit with 2 FT + 3 C. Base is $1,400,000 at 14.0%, yielding $196,000 with the same staffing count. Scaled is $2,500,000 at 20%, yielding $500,000 with 3 FT + 4 C. Total implied annual costs are therefore $276,000, $1,204,000, and $2,000,000 respectively. Those totals include vendor costs; subtracting license purchases again from the stated net profit would double count them. Conversely, license spread is not owner profit because payroll, contractors, service delivery, insurance, collections, and overhead still consume it. The staffing labels describe headcount, not five or seven fully utilized premium salaries. Validate actual hours, compensation, and owner-labor treatment before adopting the model. Gross billings are the supplied planning basis; statutory reporting may require a principal-versus-agent assessment by transaction. A commission-only arrangement does not become gross resale revenue because the customer's software spend is large. Maintain a bridge between the scorecard basis, booked revenue, supplier pass-throughs, and cash receipts so apparent growth cannot hide a deteriorating spread.

Model a marketplace transaction as a waterfall with explicitly assigned fees. On an illustrative $100,000 customer charge, assume $88,000 supplier cost, $2,000 contractually assigned marketplace and distributor charges, $3,000 delivery labor, and $1,000 sales compensation. Contribution is $6,000 before shared overhead, tax treatment, and any owner-profit adjustments. These assumed charges are not published AWS or Microsoft tariffs. If the customer receives a $5,000 credit that the supplier does not match, contribution falls to $1,000. If a separately expected $4,000 rebate is rejected, the transaction never earned that incremental amount; do not describe it as cash already secured. Store each fee against its payer, calculation base, settlement event, refund treatment, and source agreement. Currency movements, withholding, indirect taxes, and minimum distributor charges require separate fields rather than a miscellaneous percentage. Where a marketplace deducts a charge before remittance, reconcile gross customer consideration to the settlement statement and bank deposit. Where the customer purchases directly and pays the reseller only for services, exclude the vendor's license sale from reseller billings. The fallback for an unpriced fee is a corrected quote, not an assumption that implementation margin will absorb the shortfall.

Slow collections can kill a profitable model before the first renewal. At Base annual billings, average monthly sales are about $116,667. Under a simplified steady-state model in which all sales are credit sales, sixty days of receivables using annual revenue divided by 365 implies roughly $230,137 outstanding. That exceeds the upper $150,000 startup-capital reference before considering inventory-like supplier commitments or service payroll. It is exposure, not a precise funding requirement: payables, deposits, marketplace settlement mechanics, and actual sales seasonality change the cash gap. Build a thirteen-week cash forecast from dated obligations instead. A $50,000 unrecovered customer balance equals about 25.5% of Base annual owner profit if the associated costs remain payable and no recovery offsets the loss. Define credit limits using committed supplier cost plus unpaid services, less cleared deposits and contractually usable credits. Do not count a disputed rebate as available liquidity. Require intervention when projected unrestricted cash falls below the next thirty days of unavoidable obligations. Fallbacks include deposits, milestone billing, reduced incremental exposure, and vendor-approved customer-direct licensing with a separate service contract; existing service duties remain governed by their actual terms.

sections.heading: 3. Fence the 340B Workflow and Public-Sector Representations
paragraphs: The supplied play section_340b_contract_pharmacy_spread_arbitrage is a specialized customer workflow, not permission for a software reseller to acquire drugs or collect pharmacy reimbursement. Under 42 U.S.C. § 256b, eligible covered entities receive ceiling-price protections subject to statutory conditions, including diversion and duplicate-discount prohibitions. Eligibility must be established for the particular entity and relevant sites; being a rural hospital or treating an eligible population alone does not establish participation. Federally Qualified Health Centers, qualifying Ryan White entities, and hospitals must be evaluated under their applicable eligibility categories. The statutory ceiling-price formula is not a universal 25–50% discount promise, and commercial reimbursement is neither uniform nor necessarily retained in full. Manufacturer restrictions, payer adjustments, acquisition cost, dispensing costs, claim reversals, and contract terms determine actual economics. The reseller's authorized opportunity is implementing split-billing software, interfaces, reconciliation, and controlled administrative workflows. Do not book drug acquisition value, insurer reimbursement, or the covered entity's retained spread as software revenue. Require the covered entity to own patient-eligibility determinations, inventory policies, and exception resolution. Tele-referral capture cannot substitute for a qualifying care relationship or manufacture eligibility through a software flag. Test exception paths against the current program requirements and the customer's documented clinical and pharmacy operating model.

Use transparent unit economics to expose the boundary. Assume, solely for illustration, a pharmacy transaction receives $8,000 in payer and patient collections against $4,000 drug acquisition, $300 dispensing and fulfillment, and $200 other attributable expense. The remaining $3,500 belongs in the pharmacy and covered-entity contract reconciliation before further allocations; it is not reseller income. A software operator charging $30 per processed eligible claim across 200 monthly claims bills $6,000 monthly, or $72,000 annually. At $4,000 monthly directly attributable delivery cost, that example leaves $24,000 annual contribution before shared overhead, not the Conservative scenario's owner profit merely because the dollar amounts coincide. Flat fees do not automatically satisfy 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b(b); referral remuneration, federal-program business, and any applicable safe harbor require separate assessment. Do not price tele-referrals as purchased patient volume. The proposed fallback of an entity-owned specialty pharmacy requires its own licenses, payer arrangements, operational capacity, and entity-specific eligibility analysis. Automated 340B ESP submissions may support manufacturer-specific processes where required and permitted, but uploading claims does not automatically unlock restricted NDCs. If the route remains unavailable, suspend the affected workflow instead of substituting another entity's identifiers.

Data-processing and procurement failures can create losses far larger than software spread. When the reseller acts as a HIPAA business associate, execute the required agreement, bind relevant subcontractors, and implement access, audit, incident, and termination procedures appropriate to its actual role. A business-associate agreement does not itself authorize every analytics or manufacturer-data submission. Keep patient records out of ordinary partner-ticket attachments; use approved secure channels and the minimum data necessary for the task. For public procurement, verify solicitation-specific requirements, applicable contract clauses, reseller representations, and acceptance evidence. Knowingly false material claims or statements connected to government payment can implicate 31 U.S.C. § 3729; a vendor badge cannot cure a fabricated certification. FAR 52.212-4 and 52.232-25 matter only where applicable to the actual contract, and subcontract payment rights do not automatically mirror the government's obligations. A $75,000 accepted-looking invoice still creates a cash hole if the authorized buyer rejects the delivery record and the supplier has already billed $66,000. Preserve the order, authorized acceptance, license assignment, and submission receipt as distinct artifacts. If evidence is defective, correct the record and payment request rather than backdating acceptance or borrowing another partner's authorization.

sections.heading: 4. Instrument Early Warnings and Contain Failure Without Creating Another Breach
paragraphs: Build a daily exception ledger joining CRM opportunity, registration, quote revision, customer order, supplier order, subscription identifier, service ticket, invoice, settlement, and bank receipt. Salesforce or HubSpot can hold commercial records; a controlled SQL database or spreadsheet can perform the initial reconciliation without an expensive integration project. AWS Marketplace reports, Microsoft Partner Center exports, and distributor statements provide different evidence and must not be treated as interchangeable. Store original currency, transaction date, fee category, and the source document behind every adjustment. Start with operator-selected thresholds, then recalibrate using actual contract economics: review contribution erosion greater than two percentage points, receivables more than fifteen days past their contractual due date, and any registration expiring within thirty days. These are internal intervention settings, not vendor enforcement standards. A customer may legitimately have longer payment terms; measure lateness against the agreed date rather than calling every sixty-day balance delinquent. Separate leading indicators from realized losses. An unresolved license-assignment mismatch is a delivery risk; an accepted supplier credit is a potential offset; a cleared refund changes cash. Assign an owner, next action, and deadline to each exception so the dashboard produces decisions rather than a colorful backlog.

Use circuit-breakers that match the defect and avoid cascading damage. Any unverified administrative identity, exposed privileged credential, unsupported end-customer substitution, or unexplained duplicate entitlement warrants immediate security review and a hold on related new provisioning. That does not authorize disabling a customer's existing production service contrary to contract. Contain access through supported procedures, preserve evidence, and coordinate continuity with the customer and vendor. Alert when service hours exceed 110% of budget before acceptance, forecast contribution falls below the written deal floor, or conditional rebates represent more than 25% of expected transaction contribution. The rebate threshold flags dependence; it does not establish an accounting recognition rule. Where a $20,000 expected contribution includes $8,000 conditional incentives, the dependency is 40%, and the transaction must also survive the $12,000 no-incentive case. Put a separate watch on customer concentration and supplier concentration because one account's payment dispute and one vendor's policy change can hit simultaneously. When a channel account is suspended, stop offers requiring that account, secure customer records, and pursue the documented review process. Do not create nominee accounts, misrepresent ownership, or transfer transactions to hide the suspension; those shortcuts enlarge the original contractual and operational exposure.

Run a weekly loss review and a monthly reversal simulation. Take the ten largest open exposures, remove all conditional rebates, delay the largest collection by thirty days, and insert one customer refund that the supplier refuses to match. Recalculate cash, contribution, and staffing capacity without changing the published scorecard cases. These sensitivities describe resilience around the Conservative, Base, and Scaled plans; they are not replacement forecasts. Track both dollars and aging for unmatched credits, rejected incentive claims, unaccepted implementations, and vendor-policy exceptions. A falling exception count can conceal rising exposure when the remaining cases are larger. Require documentary closure: a bank receipt closes collection risk, an accepted credit closes the relevant payable adjustment, and verified customer acceptance closes that delivery milestone. A salesperson's assurance closes none of them. Retain alternate authorized distributors where commercially sensible, exportable entitlement records, and customer-specific transition instructions so vendor disruption does not become hostage-taking. Finally, compare actual profit with the $24,000, $196,000, and $500,000 annual targets using consistent cost classification. If growth requires repeated exceptions to credit, authorization, or delivery controls, reduce new commitments and repair the unit economics. More bookings cannot repair a transaction design that loses money whenever its promises are tested.

statutory_citations.title: 31 U.S.C. § 3729 — False claims
statutory_citations.relevance: Creates civil liability for specified knowing conduct involving false claims and material false records or statements; procurement certifications and acceptance evidence must remain truthful.

statutory_citations.relevance: When applicable to the contract, governs matters including inspection, acceptance, invoicing, payment, and termination; quote and delivery procedures must reflect the actual incorporated terms.

statutory_citations.relevance: When applicable, links federal payment timing to proper invoices and acceptance conditions; it does not automatically transfer identical payment rights to a reseller's subcontract.

chapters.question_prompt: Where do high-margin deals, clients, or undervalued assets hide in enterprise software reselling, and what repeatable outbound/inbound sourcing system lands the first 3-to-10 wins (3–9 months)?
chapters.title: Sourcing, Demand Mining & Landing Your First Deals
chapters.subtitle: Mine Renewal Windows, AWS CPPO and Microsoft CSP Demand with Deal Registration, License Evidence, and Procurement-Ready Implementation Scopes
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #23, Enterprise Software Reselling, ranks #14 with a 87/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter maps nine sourcing plays: renewal rescue, license reconciliation, cloud commitment alignment, security remediation, acquisition integration, public procurement, implementation recovery, vendor referral coverage, and customs-workflow modernization. Build the first three to ten wins around documented purchase events, authorized distribution, and separately priced delivery. Canonical annual owner net profits are $24,000 Conservative, $196,000 Base, and $500,000 Scaled, against gross license resale and service billings of $300,000, $1,400,000, and $2,500,000. Vendor costs remain inside the margin calculation. The operating sequence turns public signals into verified buying windows, registered opportunities, scoped implementation work, and collectible contracts without confusing customer spending or tariff exposure with reseller revenue.

sections.heading: 1. Mine Purchase Events Instead of Collecting Unqualified Names
paragraphs: Start with one buyer, one software category, and one purchase event. A workable opening wedge is a regional manufacturer with 250 to 2,000 employees, an infrastructure lead, and a renewal or integration deadline inside 180 days. Build an account ledger in HubSpot or Salesforce with legal entity, parent company, signal date, evidence URL, probable product, incumbent partner, estimated buying window, and next verification question. Use SEC EDGAR acquisition filings, SAM.gov notices, municipal purchasing portals, vendor partner directories, company engineering posts, and job advertisements naming migration responsibilities. A job advertisement proves recruiting activity, not an installed license count; a contract award proves a historical purchase, not an open renewal. Preserve that distinction in every record. Review fifty accounts weekly, retain twenty supported hypotheses, and ask a human to validate timing before assigning opportunity value. Avoid collecting personal contact details unrelated to the purchase. The best signal combines a dated operational change with an identifiable budget owner and a plausible implementation burden. A generic technology fingerprint without a deadline belongs in monitoring, not the active pipeline. Track signal age so stale evidence cannot inflate coverage. Record contradictions alongside supporting evidence rather than deleting them.

Use eight direct software plays and one adjacent customs-workflow play as the chapter's nine mapped sourcing routes. Renewal rescue starts with a verified expiration and a comparison of current entitlements against actual use. License reconciliation starts with customer-authorized exports and ends with a purchased remediation scope, not an unsolicited accusation of underlicensing. Cloud commitment alignment connects an eligible software purchase to the customer's existing marketplace procurement process, while security remediation attaches implementation to a documented control gap. Acquisition integration uses public transaction announcements to identify duplicate identity, backup, and collaboration estates. Public procurement uses published solicitations and award histories, respecting the stated communications process. Implementation recovery targets stalled deployments through customer referrals rather than public shaming. Vendor referral coverage serves territories or account sizes the publisher cannot support economically. Each route needs its own unit calculation and fallback, shown below. Treat these as sourcing hypotheses, not nine guaranteed revenue streams. The opening economics should reward a narrow specialist: one credible license analysis and one repeatable implementation package outperform a catalog containing hundreds of products nobody on the team can deploy. Do not represent informal introductions as authorized reseller status.

The supplied adjacent play, section_321_de_minimis_bonded_tariff_arbitrage, describes routing inventory through Tijuana IMMEX or Canadian bonded warehouses before individual consumer fulfillment. Do not sell its claimed tariff elimination as a current entitlement. The United States suspended duty-free de minimis treatment globally effective August 29, 2025; verify subsequent changes before designing any entry workflow. Section 321, 19 U.S.C. § 1321, is not blanket permission to divide commercial shipments, and Entry Type 86 is a filing mechanism rather than independent eligibility. For sourcing, translate the disruption into demand for customs data integration, order management, landed-cost controls, and broker exception queues. A brand shipping 10,000 monthly orders at an illustrative $4 duty exposure has $40,000 of customer exposure, not reseller revenue. Applying the historical 35–50% savings-fee concept would produce $14,000–$20,000 only if lawful, documented savings actually existed; exclude that contingent amount from this software pipeline. Instead quote a $12,000 integration with $7,000 direct delivery cost. Non-301 origin alone does not restore suspended treatment. First-sale valuation requires transaction evidence and broker review; bonded storage may defer duties rather than erase them. Fall back to ordinary duty-paid workflows when eligibility cannot be established.

callout.title: Use Channel Friction as Evidence, Not as a Sales Claim
callout.body: Experienced specialists make timing, authority, and delivery constraints visible before negotiating the headline discount.
items: Ask the customer for a redacted renewal notice before requesting publisher pricing; dates and product identifiers make registration defensible.
Request written confirmation of registration duration, protected entity, and renewal treatment; a portal submission alone does not establish protection.
Ask a distributor credit desk about required deposits before quoting payment terms; a profitable order can still exhaust available cash.
For customs-adjacent software, involve the customer's broker in data-field design and preserve ruling references instead of promising tariff savings.

sections.heading: 2. Qualify Margin, Authority, and Cash Before Building the Quote
paragraphs: Score opportunities on six dimensions totaling one hundred points: verified purchase timing twenty, budget-owner access twenty, economic spread twenty, reseller authorization fifteen, implementation fit fifteen, and collection quality ten. Award full timing points only when the customer supplies a dated renewal, purchase milestone, or published procurement schedule; a salesperson's optimism earns nothing. Give economic points against an actual distributor quote with expiry, currency, quantities, and cancellation terms. Set seventy-five points as the active pursuit threshold, but treat absent authorization or unacceptable payment exposure as disqualifying regardless of total. An opportunity scoring eighty-five with a nontransferable license cannot be repaired by enthusiasm. In the first call, ask who signs, who administers, who pays, and who can block deployment. These are often four different people. Confirm the buying entity before registering a parent company or subsidiary; publisher coverage may differ. Document the customer's reason to change partners without soliciting restricted competitor material. A qualified opportunity has a buyer-confirmed next step and a dated evidence request, not merely a friendly meeting. Recalculate the score whenever price, timing, scope, or payment terms change materially.

Separate reseller authorization from marketplace routing. AWS Marketplace channel partner private offers, commonly CPPO, require the applicable seller relationship and selling authorization; Microsoft CSP requires the relevant direct or indirect channel arrangement and customer relationship mechanics. Microsoft marketplace multiparty private offers are a separate route, not a synonym for CSP. Confirm the actual program, product, geography, buyer account, tax treatment, and settlement flow before drafting commercial promises. Deal registration can protect an opportunity or improve pricing under publisher rules, but it does not automatically override an incumbent agreement. Ask the publisher to confirm the registered legal entity and expiration in writing. For cloud commitments, have the customer verify which eligible purchases count under their specific agreement; never promise universal dollar-for-dollar treatment. The operator's worksheet should show customer price, vendor payable, platform charges, implementation labor, support reserve, and expected cash dates separately. If the operator acts only as an agent, commission revenue may be the appropriate recognition basis. Do not inflate that commission into gross resale billings merely to resemble the scorecard. Compare the canonical gross-billing cases only with transactions whose contractual and accounting treatment supports that basis.

Run a cash test before a margin test becomes a commitment. An illustrative $100,000 license order with $88,000 vendor cost has a $12,000 product spread before platform charges, labor, support, and overhead. If the vendor requires payment on day fifteen and the customer pays on day sixty, the reseller carries $88,000 for forty-five days. That single order can consume much of the canonical $15,000–$75,000 startup capital range, while monthly operating expense still runs $5,000–$25,000. Seek a deposit, shorter customer terms, distributor credit, or a permitted marketplace settlement structure; calculate each alternative from its actual contract rather than assuming immediate payout. For public buyers, follow solicitation instructions and any incorporated FAR 52.212-4 payment provisions instead of demanding terms the contract cannot support. For subscriptions, disclose term length, renewal mechanics, seat-reduction restrictions, and cancellation exposure before signature. Preserve written scope acceptance for implementation milestones. A ten-percent customer deposit does not fund an eighty-eight-percent supplier obligation. When no workable cash structure exists, offer a paid assessment or services-only delivery and let the publisher transact the license directly.

sections.heading: 3. Run a Permission-Aware Cadence That Converts Signals into Paid Discovery
paragraphs: Organize outbound around the account event rather than a scraped contact list. On day one, send a short email connecting the public signal to one operational hypothesis and ask for a fifteen-minute verification call. For an acquisition, write that duplicate identity administration often complicates integration, then ask whether consolidation is on the current plan; do not assert that the buyer has a security defect. On day three, call a published business number and leave one concise message. On day six, send a relevant implementation checklist or an anonymized scope example. On day ten, request an introduction through a publisher representative only with an appropriate relationship and without sharing customer-confidential material. On day fourteen, close the sequence with a clear choice to discuss, defer, or stop. Honor suppression across channels. Commercial email must meet 15 U.S.C. § 7704 requirements, including accurate routing information, required identification, a valid postal address, and a working opt-out honored within the statutory period. Do not treat business outreach as permission for automated calls or texts; assess those methods separately under applicable rules. Keep sequences small enough that every response receives human review.

Use an explicit funnel hypothesis to plan the first wins. Across twelve weeks, research 600 distinct accounts, retain 240 with credible purchase signals, reach 120 through delivered messages or completed introductions, conduct thirty discovery meetings, qualify fifteen opportunities, issue ten proposals, and win three contracts. Those stage conversions are 40%, 50%, 25%, 50%, approximately 67%, and 30%, respectively; the overall account-to-win rate is 0.5%. They are illustrative planning benchmarks, not observed industry averages. Define reached consistently and deduplicate companies before calculating conversion. A proposal means a priced scope with an identified buying process, not a generic brochure. A win means an executed purchase instrument accepted through the correct channel, not a verbal endorsement. With a 3–12 month first-deal window, the twelve-week cohort may produce discoveries long before bookings. Track cohorts by first signal date and report pending opportunities separately from losses. At unchanged conversion, ten wins require roughly 2,000 researched accounts, which may exceed a small team's delivery capacity. Improve qualification and referral quality before multiplying outreach. Measure elapsed days and cash collected alongside conversion so rapid signatures cannot conceal slow settlement.

Build inbound assets that answer procurement questions rather than repeat product marketing. Publish a renewal evidence checklist, a license export preparation guide, a private-offer purchasing worksheet, and an implementation acceptance template. Each asset should identify required inputs, likely bottlenecks, and the scope of a paid diagnostic. Offer a fixed $3,000 discovery engagement requiring roughly twenty delivery hours at $90 loaded hourly cost: $1,800 direct labor leaves $1,200 before selling expense and shared overhead. If that fee is later credited against implementation, record the credit so revenue is not counted twice. Keep customer production data out of public forms; request sanitized counts first and obtain authorized access only after scope agreement. Co-host narrow workshops with an authorized publisher representative or distributor specialist, using a sample environment rather than customer credentials. Tag each inquiry by asset, partner, purchase event, and verified timeline. Measure qualified discoveries per asset and gross contribution per partner referral, not download totals. For regulated or public buyers, provide procurement-ready descriptions without implying certifications or contract vehicles the business does not hold. Retire assets that attract unfunded research but no actionable purchase events.

sections.heading: 4. Close the First Wins Without Mistaking Product Spread for Owner Profit
paragraphs: Handle objections by locating the missing decision fact. When the buyer says the incumbent is cheaper, ask whether the comparison includes the same term, quantities, support, implementation, and payment conditions; reconcile those fields before discussing discount. When procurement prefers buying direct, offer a transparent services-only alternative or an eligible marketplace route, explaining the distinct operational benefit rather than inventing channel exclusivity. When the buyer asks for guaranteed commitment drawdown, obtain agreement-specific confirmation from the relevant marketplace team. When security blocks administrator access, propose customer-operated exports, temporary least-privilege access, or a supervised working session. When the sponsor wants a free proof of concept, define a paid diagnostic with acceptance criteria and an optional, explicitly priced conversion credit. When purchasing requests extended payment, price and fund that exposure or restructure the transaction. Do not accept an unfunded obligation to save a headline win. Capture the objection category, evidence supplied, commercial change, and final result in the opportunity record. Repeated losses to one issue should change the targeting or offer design, not merely lengthen the follow-up sequence. Close the loop with a written decision summary the buyer can circulate internally.

Reconcile every annual planning case to the canonical scorecard. Conservative gross license resale and service billings are $300,000; total modeled costs of $276,000 leave $24,000 owner net profit at 8%, supported by 2 FT + 3 C. Base billings are $1,400,000; total modeled costs of $1,204,000 leave $196,000 at 14.0%, again with 2 FT + 3 C. Scaled billings are $2,500,000; total modeled costs of $2,000,000 leave $500,000 at 20%, with 3 FT + 4 C, seven people. Those residual cost totals include vendor costs and all other modeled expenses; they are not separate estimates of payroll. An illustrative volume bridge is six $50,000 contracts, fourteen $100,000 contracts, or twenty-five $100,000 contracts, respectively. These are equivalent billing packages, not promises about average order size or the first selling year. The first three to ten wins establish delivery evidence and renewal cohorts; they do not automatically produce the Base case. Contractor counts do not specify full-time utilization, so budget actual hours before hiring. Do not add product spread, assessment contribution, customer cloud spend, or avoided duties to owner profit as though they were independent gains.

Close the first transaction with a delivery packet that another operator can execute without reconstructing the sale. Include the accepted quote, publisher authorization, customer purchase instrument, license quantities, tenant or account identifiers supplied through an authorized channel, implementation scope, acceptance tests, support boundaries, and collection schedule. Confirm whether signature, marketplace acceptance, purchase order, or another event actually forms the order under the governing documents. After provisioning, reconcile ordered versus delivered entitlements and obtain customer confirmation of the configured outcome. Schedule renewal alerts at 180, 120, 90, and 60 days, adjusted to contractual notice requirements. Automate quote assembly and license reconciliation only after the underlying fields have accountable owners; automation cannot repair an incorrect product identifier or unauthorized discount. Request a reference after demonstrated value and ask permission before sharing any customer-identifying material. Hold a weekly review of stage aging, expected contribution, cash exposure, delivery capacity, and publisher policy changes. During months three through twelve, favor repeatable wins inside the selected specialty over unrelated catalog expansion. A renewal-ready customer with clean entitlements and collectible invoices is a stronger asset than a large unscoped order requiring continual founder intervention.

chapters.question_prompt: How does an operator execute enterprise software reselling end-to-end from intake to reconciled cash, backed by an auditable technical/ledger blueprint and a worked 90-day cohort walk?
chapters.title: The Complete Operating Process, Production Blueprint & 90-Day Cohort Walk
chapters.subtitle: AWS CPPO, Microsoft CSP, Deal Registration, SQLite Evidence Controls, and Cash-to-Ledger Reconciliation
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #23, Enterprise Software Reselling, ranks #14 with a 87/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter connects nine mapped plays to one controlled operating system: qualify demand, establish channel rights, price vendor obligations, deliver accepted scope, and reconcile collected cash. Eight chapter-defined channel plays accompany the supplied customs integration play; customer tariff savings never become reseller revenue automatically. The canonical annual owner profits are $24,000 Conservative, $196,000 Base, and $500,000 Scaled. A six-module SQLite reference separates evidence, offer dispatch, and balanced postings. A worked mature-pipeline quarter produces $350,000 gross resale and service revenue, $49,000 owner profit, and $24,000 operating cash generation, explicitly bridging the Base annual run rate without pretending a new reseller closes immediately.

sections.heading: 1. Convert nine mapped plays into authorized, collectible orders
paragraphs: Start with the commercial relationship, not the quotation screen. Record the customer legal entity, tenant identifier, procurement contact, beneficial contracting party, renewal date, product edition, seat count, and deployment geography in Salesforce or HubSpot. Attach the current distributor agreement and the vendor's authorization record before representing a resale right. For AWS Marketplace channel partner private offers, distinguish the independent software vendor's selling authorization from the customer's acceptance of your private offer. For Microsoft CSP, distinguish direct billing from an indirect provider relationship and record the applicable subscription cancellation window. Neither a registered opportunity nor a generated quote proves entitlement. Score demand using documented authority, delivery feasibility, collection risk, and contribution after vendor commitments. An attractive percentage spread can conceal a disastrous payment mismatch: a $100,000 annual license with $82,000 due upstream immediately requires substantial working capital when the customer pays after sixty days. Capture that exposure before assigning a probability-weighted pipeline value. The first full-time operator owns commercial evidence; the second owns delivery and reconciliation. Contractors receive bounded implementation work, never uncontrolled permission to change price, payee details, or customer licensing. Keep approvals and artifact versions attached to the same immutable deal reference.

The nine-play map below is an operating taxonomy, not an assertion that nine external catalog identifiers were supplied. Eight chapter-defined channel plays cover intake, registration, CPPO, CSP, implementation, renewal, entitlement reconciliation, and collections. The ninth preserves the supplied customs_first_sale_rule_valuation_arbitrage identifier as an adjacent customer integration opportunity. Every play must end with a priced deliverable, a cost owner, and a documented fallback. A $100,000 resale with an $82,000 vendor charge creates $18,000 before implementation, marketplace charges, credit losses, and overhead; it does not create $100,000 of profit. Likewise, a $20,000 migration performed with $12,000 of contractor effort creates an $8,000 delivery contribution before shared costs. Maintain separate quote lines for licenses, services, support, taxes, and customer-specific pass-through amounts. The scorecard uses gross license resale and service billings with vendor costs inside margin. Actual reporting still requires a principal-versus-agent assessment under the applicable accounting framework; an agent arrangement cannot simply adopt gross presentation because the scorecard does. Compare like arrangements when measuring progress against the Base case. Keep the example ticket economics separate from the quarter model rather than silently blending their cost ratios into its results.

For the customs adjacency, sell secure document integration and workflow configuration, not a promised tariff outcome. Under 19 U.S.C. 1401a and 19 CFR 152.103, qualifying transaction value depends on the underlying sale and required additions. Nissho Iwai American Corp. v. United States, 982 F.2d 505, describes conditions relevant to using an earlier sale, including clear destination and arm's-length evidence; a cheaper invoice alone does not establish eligibility. At one million units, $18 per unit produces $18 million of importer invoices while $8 produces $8 million of factory value. At an illustrative uniform 10% duty, the arithmetic difference is $1 million, or 55.6% of the original $1.8 million duty. Assists, royalties, freight treatment, product classifications, and other duties can change that result; a 35–55% sales claim is not an operating assumption. Use an encrypted customs-broker evidence vault, preserve CBP access, and require a transaction-specific customs-counsel opinion before supporting the customer's filing workflow. The buyer need not receive unrestricted factory invoices merely because the integration accesses them. If evidence fails, retain the supported valuation method and pause the savings claim. A separately contracted $15,000 integration remains reseller service revenue; the customer's duty reduction remains theirs.

callout.title: Protect the spread before chasing the signature
callout.body: Experienced channel operators preserve evidence and working capital before counting a signed order as a successful deal.
items: Set quote expiration earlier than the earliest vendor price, currency, or deal-registration expiration; an accepted customer price must not outlive its supply economics.
For CPPO, retain the selling authorization identifier alongside the accepted offer identifier; those records prove different commercial facts.
For CSP, export subscription terms and quantities before each change request, then compare the provider's resulting charge rather than trusting the interface preview.
Keep factory invoices inside the broker-controlled vault; sell the integration milestone and never invoice the customer's modeled tariff savings as license revenue.

sections.heading: 2. Build the evidence ledger and serialize irreversible transitions
paragraphs: The six modules below form a compact SQLite reference, supplied as executable source strings in execution order. Save each code cell into one local script, or concatenate them in order, and run with Python 3.9 or later. They use only standard-library components and create a local ledger.sqlite3 database. This reference has not been executed in this chapter. Test it against a disposable database before adapting it to production. SQLite runs on a local persistent disk with one connection per worker, foreign keys enabled, and explicit write transactions. Every read-modify-write operation obtains BEGIN IMMEDIATE before examining mutable state. Concurrent writers therefore serialize or receive a bounded lock error; callers retry the whole transaction with the same business key, never a partial write. Unique constraints provide a second defense against duplicated intake, state transitions, commands, and ledger postings. Hashes detect request substitution, not document authenticity. Store actual contracts in an encrypted, access-controlled object store such as Amazon S3 with versioning and retention configured for the engagement. Keep its immutable version reference and content digest in the evidence record. Do not place credentials, factory invoices, or customer personal records inside quote payloads or application logs.

The state machine separates intake, verified authority, evidence-ready status, queued offer, booked acceptance, and reconciled cash. The evidence-ready state is the workflow's escrow checkpoint: protected documents are available to authorized reviewers, not customer funds held by the reseller. An authorized reviewer checks the source artifacts before recording each evidence reference. The example intake score merely prioritizes cases; its Boolean fields do not authenticate a vendor authorization. Transitions use an expected prior state and return harmlessly only when the same completed transition carries the same evidence. Different evidence on a reused transition produces an error for investigation. The outbox reserves a command and marks it sending before any external request. A second worker cannot claim that command. A crash after reservation intentionally leaves work unresolved rather than assuming that no offer was created. An operator or adapter must look up the external result using the stable request reference. Where a vendor endpoint supports documented idempotency, pass that key; where it does not, do not automatically resubmit an ambiguous request. Local serialization eliminates local check-then-act races, but cannot manufacture an exactly-once guarantee across an uncooperative remote service.

The accounting representation uses transfers with equal debit and credit amounts, so every stored row balances by construction. A single posting batch is atomic, amounts are positive integer cents, and each source reference has an immutable payload. Book earned gross billings as a receivable debit and revenue credit; book vendor expense against payables when the obligation is incurred. Customer receipts debit cash and credit receivables. Vendor payments debit payables and credit cash. Contractor delivery and operating expenses remain separate accounts, allowing the cohort's contribution and owner-profit bridge to be reproduced without a spreadsheet override. Post corrections as new reversing transfers, never edits to earlier rows. The view exposes signed account balances by deal and calendar month; collection closure additionally requires invoice totals to match the accepted quote and receivables to reach zero. A bank evidence reference still requires human or authenticated feed verification outside this reference. Restrict production database writes to the service account, back up the database with SQLite's backup API, and test restoration. Triggers guard against accidental mutation, not a privileged administrator. Archive reviewed bank statements independently so database integrity and cash existence have separate evidence sources.

callout.body: The reference intentionally stops short of live vendor calls. Complete these checks before connecting an authorized adapter.
items: Confirm current reseller authorization, distributor payment terms, product geography, customer tenant, and the specific buyer's contracting authority.
Run two separate worker processes against the same disposable database; verify one intake row, one outbox reservation, and one posting per source reference.

Restore a backup, compare ledger balances to independent bank evidence, and prove the operator can retrieve each encrypted contract version without exposing another customer's records.

sections.heading: 3. Walk a mature pipeline through ninety days of profit and cash
paragraphs: The Worked 90-Day Cohort Walk models a quarter from an established, authorized reseller with an already mature pipeline. It is not a claim that cold leads routinely become enterprise cash inside ninety days. The canonical time to first deal is three to twelve months, so a new operator uses this period to establish authorization, evidence controls, relationships, and implementation capability while funding a longer sales cycle. The walk opens with $75,000 cash contributed by the owner, within the $15,000–$75,000 startup range, and zero receivables or vendor payables. That contribution credits equity, not revenue. Month 1 processes forty opportunities: eight are scrubbed for eligibility, twenty are lost, four become accepted deals, and eight remain open. Month 2 processes fifty distinct opportunities with ten scrubs, twenty-four losses, six accepted deals, and ten open. Month 3 processes sixty with twelve scrubs, thirty losses, seven accepted deals, and eleven open. These are separate intake cohorts, so open opportunities are not counted again as fresh leads. Their future value is excluded from the quarter's recognized revenue. A scrub means evidence or fit failed before booking; a loss means an eligible opportunity did not close.

Accepted and earned gross billings are $80,000, $120,000, and $150,000 by month. Month 1 has four $20,000 tickets, Month 2 has six, and Month 3 has six $20,000 tickets plus one $30,000 ticket. For this example, each accepted package satisfies its applicable recognition conditions in its booking month; unperformed future services would instead require a different schedule. License and cloud resale contribute $280,000 of quarter revenue and accepted implementation services contribute $70,000. Vendor expense totals $245,000, contractor delivery expense $21,000, and operating expense $35,000. Operating expense covers the modeled two full-time roles and shared systems; three contractors are part-time capacity whose billed delivery is already in contractor expense. Do not count their hours again in overhead. Monthly operating expense is $11,000, $12,000, and $12,000, inside the canonical $5,000–$25,000 range. Monthly owner profit is consequently $8,200, $16,800, and $24,000. The quarter produces exactly $49,000 on $350,000 gross revenue, a 14.0% margin. Annualizing the whole quarter by four yields $1,400,000 revenue and $196,000 owner profit; annualizing the strongest month would misrepresent the Base case and should not appear in the dashboard.

Cash follows a different timetable. Collect $60,000 of Month 1 invoices during Month 1. During Month 2 collect the remaining $20,000 from that cohort and $80,000 from Month 2 invoices. During Month 3 collect Month 2's remaining $40,000 and $110,000 from Month 3 invoices. Quarter receipts therefore equal $310,000, with $40,000 still receivable. Vendor obligations accrue at $56,000, $84,000, and $105,000, but cash payments are $40,000, $80,000, and $110,000. Clear the oldest vendor invoices first, leaving $15,000 payable at quarter end. Pay delivery expense and overhead within each month. Operating cash generation becomes $4,200, $800, and $19,000; cumulative operating cash is $24,000. The independent bridge is $49,000 profit minus the $40,000 receivables increase plus the $15,000 payables increase. Closing cash is $99,000 after the opening equity contribution. No sales taxes, financing charges, owner distributions, refunds, or unearned customer advances are assumed; adding any requires additional postings and a revised bridge. If vendor terms require earlier payment, change the cash schedule immediately rather than preserving the model by overdue payments. Maintain a reserve against the actual upstream commitments, not merely the next payroll date.

sections.heading: 4. Operate exception queues, statutory duties, and controlled scaling
paragraphs: Run a daily exception review from records, not optimistic sales commentary. The commercial operator examines expiring registrations, authorization changes, unaccepted offers, procurement holds, and overdue receivables. The delivery operator examines tenant mismatches, missing entitlement exports, unsigned acceptance tests, contractor overruns, and unresolved sending commands. Each exception receives an owner, monetary exposure, next action, and due date. A license reconciliation exception might expose ten unwanted seats at $30 per month; that is $300 of monthly exposure, not a reason to invent a completed customer cancellation. A vendor policy change can invalidate a previously sound quote, so suspend new offers for the affected product while preserving already accepted contractual obligations. For collections, distinguish an administrative purchase-order problem from a disputed delivery milestone before sending reminders. Use bank-provided remittance evidence, not a customer's email screenshot, to clear cash. Separate the person changing payee bank details from the person releasing vendor payment. Confirm changes through a previously established contact channel. The two-person core team can support that separation if duties are scheduled explicitly and contractor access remains limited to assigned delivery artifacts rather than unrestricted billing or treasury functions.

Apply statutory requirements to the actual transaction. For federal commercial-product purchases, FAR 12.212 addresses commercial computer software licensing, while FAR 52.212-4 supplies contract terms when incorporated into the award. Capture the actual order's acceptance, invoice, payment, and modification requirements instead of assuming that a private-sector statement of work controls. The Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act, 15 U.S.C. 7001, generally prevents denying legal effect solely because a signature or record is electronic; it does not establish that the signer had procurement authority. Preserve the identity evidence, signed version, timestamps, and retrievable record. Where California Civil Code 1798.100(d) applies to a covered business's disclosure to a service provider or contractor, the contract must include the required purpose restrictions and protection obligations. Map those duties to ticket access, retention, deletion, and subcontractor permissions. For customs integrations, preserve records required by 19 CFR Part 163 and route valuation decisions through the importer and authorized broker. These are distinct responsibilities: software access does not confer customs filing authority, and a reseller authorization does not confer permission to process every category of customer data. Resolve the specific scope before provisioning production access.

Scale only after the exception workload and cash conversion support the next commitment. The Conservative case is $300,000 annual gross revenue at 8%, leaving $24,000 owner profit with two full-time people and three contractors. The Base case is $1,400,000 at 14.0%, leaving $196,000 with that same headcount structure. The Scaled case is $2,500,000 at 20%, leaving $500,000 with three full-time people and four contractors. These are separate canonical outcomes, not evidence that adding seats automatically improves economics. The Scaled cost envelope is $2,000,000, compared with $1,204,000 at Base and $276,000 Conservative. Require an explicit vendor, delivery, and overhead budget before claiming that envelope is attainable. Automate renewal alerts, quote generation, and license reconciliation first because each reduces recurring clerical work without transferring contracting judgment to a script. Track quote corrections, unmatched entitlements, disputed acceptances, overdue cash, and manual recovery time. If the team cannot close the books and resolve exceptions within its staffed capacity, narrow product breadth before hiring around broken processes. Keep the quarter model as a reproducible test fixture: a pricing change, new payment term, or contractor rate change must flow through both owner profit and working-capital calculations.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #23, Enterprise Software Reselling, ranks #14 with a 87/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Its information advantage comes from connecting procurement evidence to authorized channel economics, not collecting indiscriminate contact lists. This chapter maps nine plays: public-award timing, entity verification, deal-registration protection, AWS CPPO private offers, Microsoft CSP provisioning, renewal rescue, license reconciliation, implementation spreads, and commercial VCC settlement rebates. An eighteen-source directory specifies access, cost structure, refresh behavior, request discipline, and fallback evidence. The canonical annual owner profits remain $24,000 Conservative, $196,000 Base, and $500,000 Scaled, calculated on gross license resale and service billings with vendor costs included. Public records prioritize investigation; partner permissions, customer authorization, accepted offers, and reconciled settlements establish what the desk can actually sell and collect.

sections.heading: 1. Build an eighteen-source directory around evidence the desk can use
paragraphs: Start with the buying event, not the email address. The public-award timing play connects SAM.gov opportunity notices, USAspending award records, and the buyer's published procurement calendar to a specific software requirement. Capture notice identifier, agency, incumbent, contract vehicle, period of performance, option language, and source retrieval time. An award ceiling is neither available budget nor reseller revenue; obligations, modifications, and option exercises answer different questions. For an illustrative prospecting batch, twenty relevant awards producing four qualified $25,000 opportunities create $100,000 of prospective gross billings, not booked sales. A contracting officer's current solicitation outranks an enrichment vendor's inferred renewal date. FAR 4.1102 governs when prospective contractors generally need SAM registration, subject to its exceptions; registration alone does not confer a contract vehicle, publisher authorization, or permission to sell through another contractor's schedule. When an award description is sparse, follow the linked notice and agency documents before approaching the incumbent's customer. For state and municipal demand, use the issuing authority's procurement portal and appropriation documents instead of assuming federal coverage. Store the exact passage supporting the trigger so the salesperson can distinguish a funded requirement from a broad strategic aspiration.

The entity and buying-center verification play prevents a surprisingly expensive class of channel errors: registering the wrong subsidiary, quoting the wrong tenant, or confusing a distributor with the end customer. Join records using UEI, CIK, legal entity name, registered address, verified domain, and customer-confirmed billing entity; never let a domain match silently merge two companies. Delaware's entity search supplies formation clues, while paid status products answer different questions; neither reveals a complete corporate buying hierarchy. SEC submissions can establish public-company identity and published acquisitions, but a filing is not evidence that every subsidiary shares a software agreement. Use ICANN Lookup to inspect registration metadata where available, remembering that redaction and privacy services limit attribution. A fifty-account review at six minutes per account consumes five analyst hours; budget that work before buying thousands of enriched contacts. Record conflicting evidence and ask the customer which entity owns the tenant and purchase order. If the subsidiary relationship remains unresolved, retain separate account records and suspend only the affected quote. This keeps clean opportunities moving without manufacturing certainty. The fallback is a customer-issued ordering document and publisher account confirmation, not a guessed parent-company relationship derived from branding.

Use the directory below as an access register, not a promise that every source exposes a public API or a fixed refresh interval. Free access often still requires an account, API key, registered application, or restricted role. Paid enrichment plans change; record the actual subscribed quota and unit price rather than hard-coding a promotional tariff. Separate source publication delay from the desk's polling interval: polling an award feed hourly cannot accelerate an agency's reporting. Every connector should retain request time, source update time when supplied, response status, pagination cursor, and permitted retention period. Honor Retry-After, use exponential backoff with jitter, and cap concurrent requests per credential. Never rotate identities to evade a limit. For browser-only partner workspaces, use permitted exports or human review instead of undocumented automation. Cache stable identifiers, but recheck permissions and commercial terms before each offer. The nine mapped plays in this chapter are operational workflows; only the VCC play carries the supplied machine identifier. Their unit examples explain decision mechanics and are not additional scorecard forecasts. Assign one owner to each connector so a broken feed produces a visible exception rather than silently aging prospect records.

Use authorized cost exports and finalized invoices; preliminary usage should not be treated as a settled customer receivable.
