Use https://YOUR_INSTANCE.my.salesforce.com/services/data/ to discover supported versions; API availability depends on purchased edition, licenses, and organization settings.
Use incremental queries or entitled events; inspect the selected version's limits resource and response headers before scheduling bulk synchronization.
Import controlled CSV exports with stable external identifiers; do not overwrite salesperson decisions merely because enrichment returned a different value.
People Data Labs Company Enrichment supplies commercial firmographic matching candidates.
GET https://api.peopledatalabs.com/v5/company/enrich with a licensed API key; paid credit plans and any trial allowance follow current account terms.
Enrich after public identity checks and cache permitted results; provider sourcing has variable age. Enforce credit ceilings and returned rate-limit headers.
Use the company's published website and official entity records; inferred attributes require verification before affecting account ownership or eligibility.
Hunter Domain Search helps identify published business-contact patterns for verified companies.
GET https://api.hunter.io/v2/domain-search with an account API key; free allowance and paid credit tiers follow the subscribed plan.
Run only after domain verification and deduplicate requests; source dates can differ from retrieval dates. Respect account quotas and response limits.
Use the company's published contact page and switchboard; a returned address neither establishes buying authority nor authorizes indiscriminate outreach.
ICANN Lookup supplies registration-data context for domain identity investigations.
Search https://lookup.icann.org through the public interface; lookup is free, and underlying RDAP availability varies by registry.
Check during account onboarding or suspicious domain changes; registry publication controls freshness. Respect upstream limits and avoid repeated exhaustive searches.
Compare customer-confirmed domains and official company websites; redacted registration data cannot establish beneficial ownership or tenant control.

sections.heading: 2. Turn authorized channel evidence into defensible quotes and renewal actions
paragraphs: The deal-registration protection play starts with publisher rules, accepted registration status, covered account, eligible products, expiration, and named channel owner. Attach those facts to the opportunity before producing a price. One hundred seats at $200 monthly produces $240,000 of annual gross billings; at an illustrative $180 monthly vendor cost, the license spread is $24,000 before support, commissions, payment costs, and overhead. A registration discount can change that spread, but a submitted form does not earn it. Detect duplicate customer identifiers, expired protection, geography restrictions, and opportunities already held by another partner. When protection fails, ask the publisher for written terms or quote the unprotected economics; do not preserve an expired discount inside a spreadsheet. The AWS CPPO private-offer play adds a separate chain: publisher selling authorization, permitted buyer, wholesale economics, reseller offer, acceptance, and settlement. An illustrative $100,000 customer offer against $88,000 publisher cost leaves $12,000 before marketplace charges and delivery expenses. Validate which party bears each charge and whether credits reduce proceeds. Capture immutable offer and agreement identifiers rather than screenshots alone. If the authorization disappears before acceptance, stop that offer and obtain renewed terms or use a publisher-approved alternative route.

The Microsoft CSP provisioning play needs distributor or direct-bill evidence, customer agreement status, subscription term, billing frequency, cancellation window, and tenant-specific authorization. Annual commitment and monthly payment are different fields: monthly collection does not necessarily remove annual vendor liability. Two hundred seats at $30 monthly produces $72,000 annual gross billings; an illustrative $66,000 vendor invoice leaves $6,000 before operating expenses. Model a late-paying customer against the actual supplier due date, not the customer's preferred payment schedule. The renewal rescue play joins the original accepted order to current subscription records and customer-confirmed renewal intent. One hundred annual seats at $500 represent $50,000 of renewal billings, not $50,000 of profit. Schedule ninety-, sixty-, and thirty-day tasks where the actual commitment allows those interventions, then calculate the last effective change date from the current contract. Keep commercial data collection separate from workload administration; Partner Center visibility does not replace customer authorization for Graph access. Use granular delegated roles where supported and revoke unused relationships. When API evidence conflicts with the distributor's invoice, preserve both records, suspend the disputed adjustment, and resolve the mismatch before promising a cancellation, credit, or seat reduction.

The license reconciliation play compares purchased capacity, assigned seats, disabled accounts, group-based allocation, and customer-approved usage evidence without equating absence of one signal with absence of business need. Twenty removable seats at $40 monthly imply $9,600 of annual customer savings only when the commitment permits reduction. That savings figure is not operator revenue, and seat removal can reduce the reseller's own recurring spread. Charge for the assessment or expand implementation work only under an agreed statement of work. The implementation-spreads play converts verified entitlement gaps into scoped delivery: eighty hours billed at $175 yields $14,000 of service billings; eighty delivery hours costing $100 yields $8,000 of direct cost and a $6,000 contribution before overhead. Define migration batches, identity prerequisites, rollback procedures, acceptance tests, and customer responsibilities. Keep change orders separate from the original estimate. Diagnostic tools should answer concrete questions: Graph identifies entitlement discrepancies, Azure Cost Management identifies consumption patterns, and a customer-approved export establishes the baseline when API access is unavailable. Never purchase a broad administrative role merely to simplify discovery. If usage telemetry is restricted, deliver an entitlement-only assessment and identify the missing evidence explicitly rather than inventing utilization percentages.

Monthly customer billing can mask annual vendor exposure and make an apparently flexible cancellation expensive.
Confirm current publisher rules and distributor terms; obtain customer authorization before any permitted subscription change.
License assignment inventory: identify removable capacity without disrupting necessary business access.
Compare purchased capacity, assignments, group rules, account status, customer confirmation, and permitted reduction date.
Removing seats from sparse telemetry can interrupt service while contractual charges continue through the committed term.
Use a customer-reviewed exception list and reversible assignment changes; retain before-and-after inventory snapshots.
Implementation work package: establish the billable scope and direct delivery exposure.
Join signed scope, hourly assumptions, named deliverables, subcontractor rates, acceptance tests, and change-order identifiers.
Unpriced migration exceptions consume the projected service spread and turn license profit into delivery losses.
Pause only the affected work package, document the dependency, and price the approved change before continuing.

callout.title: Protect the small details that determine whether the spread survives
callout.body: Channel profit usually fails at a join between commercial records, not at the headline discount.
items: Save the publisher authorization and accepted registration version used for every quote; a later portal view may no longer show the original economics.
Store subscription commitment length separately from invoice frequency so monthly collection never disguises annual vendor exposure.
Put the last effective renewal-change date on the CRM task, not merely the service anniversary; derive it from the current agreement.
Reconcile marketplace deductions against the specific offer and settlement period before paying sales commissions on apparent spread.

sections.heading: 3. Engineer a provenance-first enrichment waterfall and exception pipeline
paragraphs: Build the enrichment waterfall in this order: customer-provided identity, official entity evidence, company-published domain and buying context, licensed company enrichment, then targeted contact discovery. Reject the common shortcut of enriching a guessed domain and treating the returned person as proof of account ownership. Every field needs source URL or request reference, retrieval time, source date when available, confidence rationale, usage restriction, and verification owner. Keep source observations immutable; materialize the preferred account view separately so an analyst can reverse an incorrect merge. A practical record contains legal_entity_id, domain, tenant_id, publisher_customer_id, opportunity_id, observed_at, and evidence_reference. Encrypt customer identifiers, restrict exports, and exclude tokens from logs. For an illustrative waterfall, researching 200 accounts with official and customer records might resolve 140; enriching the remaining 60 at an assumed $0.50 per successful lookup costs $30 before contact discovery. Those figures are workload assumptions, not vendor tariffs. If confidence remains weak, route the account to manual review rather than repeatedly purchasing the same ambiguous match. Apply provider retention terms to cached data and record deletion deadlines. A cheap enrichment credit becomes expensive when it creates a duplicate registration, misdirected quote, or avoidable customer complaint.

Implement the first pipeline with Python's urllib.request, json, sqlite3, datetime, hashlib, and logging modules, or use the same controls in an existing integration platform. Separate connectors from normalization, identity resolution, and business actions. A successful HTTP response is not proof of complete ingestion: validate required fields, traverse pagination, record counts, and persist the last completed checkpoint only after committing the batch. Use stable source identifiers plus payload hashes to make reruns idempotent. Preserve raw responses only where the license permits retention, and redact credentials before storage. For time-based queries, overlap the previous window and deduplicate because late updates and clock differences otherwise create gaps. Handle deletions and revoked permissions as explicit states rather than silently retaining stale authority. A failed connector must not erase the last verified customer record. Alert on authentication failures, repeated throttling, schema drift, empty-result anomalies, and unusual record-count changes. When a provider changes an endpoint, freeze automated quote inputs from that connector while allowing unrelated workflows to continue. Keep secrets in the organization's selected secret store, scope keys narrowly, and test rotation. Operators need evidence of freshness and completeness, not a decorative dashboard that remains green after a partial import.

Make the output a queue of decisions, not a warehouse of interesting facts. Each exception should name the customer, conflicting evidence, affected commercial action, accountable person, due time, and recovery instruction. A renewal alert without a verified commitment date should request verification, not automatically send a price. A license mismatch should produce a reviewable delta, not silently remove access. Run contract tests against retained, sanitized fixtures covering pagination, expired credentials, repeated events, changed field types, and revoked customer permissions. Measure match accuracy on a manually adjudicated sample and track false positives separately from unresolved records. For outreach, 15 U.S.C. 7704 establishes requirements including accurate headers, nondeceptive subjects, sender identification, a valid postal address, and a working opt-out mechanism where applicable; suppress opted-out recipients across every connected sending tool. If a covered business processes California residents' personal information, map applicable duties under Cal. Civ. Code 1798.100 to collection, retention, and contracted service-provider processing. Public availability does not erase provider terms or relevant privacy duties. Use role-based access and short retention for contact exports. If the desk cannot explain why a field is needed for a live account action, stop collecting it and simplify the pipeline.

sections.heading: 4. Underwrite the VCC extension without confusing payment volume with reseller revenue
paragraphs: The ninth mapped play, b2b_commercial_vcc_interchange_rebate_arbitrage, embeds an automated accounts payable and vendor-settlement service beside the software relationship. Freight brokers, construction general contractors, medical suppliers, property managers, and media agencies can have substantial third-party invoice flows, but invoice volume belongs to their payment operation, not the reseller's top line. Work through an authorized issuing and payment-platform partner; the software desk should not assume custody of customer funds or issuing authority. The play's 140–195 basis-point rebate range is a commercial underwriting assumption requiring a signed schedule, eligible volume definition, exclusions, chargeback treatment, and payout timing. It is not a universal network entitlement or a promise of uncapped earnings. At $10,000,000 of eligible settled invoices, 175 basis points produces $175,000 of platform-level rebate before contractual adjustments. If the desk receives a contracted forty-percent share, its potential receipts are $70,000 before its own costs, not $10,000,000 and not the full $175,000. Verify whether the agreement treats those receipts as service compensation or another accounting category. This optional sandbox example is excluded from the canonical resale and services scorecard. A rejected card authorization, reversed invoice, or ineligible merchant must reduce the eligible-volume ledger.

Build a vendor acceptance waterfall before selling instant settlement. Start with the customer's authorized AP export, deduplicate vendor identities, verify invoice approval and beneficiary details through established controls, and segment existing card acceptance. Request the platform's documented APIs for card creation, transaction webhooks, settlement reports, and rebate statements; account access and permitted fields depend on the actual contract. Bind each single-use credential to the intended invoice, amount, expiry, and supported merchant controls without storing sensitive card data in the CRM. The specified fallback injects Level-3 line-item invoice metadata where the issuer, processor, merchant, and network support it; metadata alone neither forces acceptance nor guarantees qualification. For card-averse suppliers, offer an agreed early-pay ACH discount of 1.5%–2% for payment within ten days against a clearly stated original due date. On a $100,000 invoice, that is $1,500–$2,000 of supplier-funded discount before funding and platform costs; allocate the benefit according to contract rather than claiming it all as desk income. Focus acquisition on fragmented long-tail vendor bases, but validate actual acceptance with a small authorized cohort. If early payment consumes working capital, price that cost and retain ordinary ACH as the no-discount fallback.

Keep the scorecard anchored while the data stack expands. Conservative remains $300,000 gross license resale and service billings multiplied by 8%, producing $24,000 annual owner net profit with 2 FT + 3 C. Base remains $1,400,000 multiplied by 14.0%, producing $196,000 with 2 FT + 3 C. Scaled remains $2,500,000 multiplied by 20%, producing $500,000 with 3 FT + 4 C. Vendor costs are already included in those margins; do not subtract them again or add client cloud consumption, AP principal, customer savings, and marketplace commitments to revenue. The directory is an operating architecture, not evidence that any scenario has been achieved. Track software spread, implementation contribution, tool subscriptions, contractor expense, bad debt, and collection timing in separate reconciled accounts. Gross presentation also requires review of whether the desk controls the promised goods or services before transfer; a marketplace label alone does not settle principal-versus-agent treatment. Respect the $15,000–$75,000 startup capital range, $5,000–$25,000 monthly operating expense range, and three-to-twelve-month first-deal horizon when buying tools. Start with official records and existing partner exports, then purchase enrichment only when a measured bottleneck justifies it. Scale connector coverage after match quality and collected contribution improve, not because a vendor dashboard displays more accounts.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #23, Enterprise Software Reselling, holds Rank #14 with a 87/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter turns contract discipline into operating controls across nine mapped plays: reseller authorization, deal registration, AWS CPPO, Microsoft CSP, implementation spreads, renewal management, license reconciliation, public-sector procurement, and authorized high-risk payment orchestration. Separate permission to sell from permission to provision, process data, or route payments. Preserve the scorecard's gross license resale and service billing basis: $300,000 at 8% produces $24,000 annual owner profit; $1,400,000 at 14.0% produces $196,000; $2,500,000 at 20% produces $500,000. Vendor costs remain inside those margins. Use signed authority, measurable acceptance, documented outreach, and bounded liability to protect each spread before committing working capital.

sections.heading: 1. Prove the right to sell before registering, quoting, or provisioning
paragraphs: Build an authority packet for each vendor, distributor, product family, territory, and selling entity. A partner badge does not establish authority to resell every SKU, issue sublicenses, access customer tenants, or appoint subagents. Save the executed channel agreement, distributor appointment, current product schedule, territory restrictions, customer eligibility rules, and dated deal-registration acknowledgment. Record expiration and termination effects in Salesforce or HubSpot, with the source document attached rather than summarized from memory. Copyright rights under 17 U.S.C. § 106 and the limited distribution rule in § 109 do not create a general right to transfer subscription credentials or duplicate software. The ownership-versus-license distinction and the actual transaction terms matter. Use vendor-approved transfers rather than selling spare tenant accounts. For a hypothetical $100,000 license order with an $82,000 vendor commitment, the $18,000 initial spread exists only if the customer is eligible and the vendor honors the quoted buy price. If authority cannot be evidenced, stop provisioning and use an authorized referral arrangement with separately documented compensation. Never represent referral status as resale authority, and never count the customer's entire purchase as referral revenue.

Treat AWS Channel Partner Private Offers and Microsoft Cloud Solution Provider transactions as different contract stacks, not interchangeable checkout buttons. For CPPO, verify the software vendor's selling authorization, permitted buyer, offer terms, wholesale economics, and marketplace settlement mechanics against the applicable agreements. For CSP, distinguish direct-bill and indirect-reseller responsibilities, the distributor relationship, customer agreement acceptance, subscription term, and the relevant cancellation window. New Commerce commitments can leave the reseller owing a distributor after customer nonpayment; a monthly customer invoice does not necessarily mean a monthly cancellable vendor obligation. Illustratively, $120,000 customer billings minus $100,000 vendor charges leave $20,000 before platform charges, delivery, financing costs, and overhead. Record who invoices, who collects, who issues credits, and who bears refunds. The scorecard uses gross resale and service billings, but statutory reporting still requires a principal-versus-agent assessment for each arrangement. If the business acts only as an agent, do not force marketplace transaction value into recognized revenue. Reconcile that difference explicitly rather than silently changing the scorecard's economic basis. Capture the accepted offer identifier, buyer account, entitlement dates, and settlement report before marking the opportunity fulfilled.

Map nine plays into distinct permission and evidence requirements: reseller authorization, deal registration, CPPO, CSP, implementation spreads, renewal management, license reconciliation, public-sector procurement, and authorized payment orchestration. Eight are ordinary channel workstreams; the ninth is an adjacent, separately controlled integration opportunity, not implied permission to acquire merchants. For deal registration, a $60,000 order bought at $48,000 yields a $12,000 initial spread; losing a $3,000 registration benefit reduces that spread to $9,000. Require written protection dates and a documented fallback quote before presenting the discount. Protect customer-specific opportunities through narrow, time-limited non-circumvention provisions that identify the introduced account and preserve existing relationships. Do not exchange future pricing with rival resellers or coordinate customer allocation; Sherman Act § 1 applies independently of partner program labels. Screen international transactions for applicable export controls and sanctions, including product classification, destination, end user, and end use. An offshore buyer is not automatically prohibited, and a domestic billing address does not settle the analysis. Preserve screening evidence and escalate unresolved restrictions before releasing keys, credentials, technical assistance, or controlled software. A distributor's willingness to invoice does not replace your own duties.

sections.heading: 2. Write contracts that protect spread, acceptance, and collection
paragraphs: Use a contract stack with a reseller master agreement, transaction order, implementation statement of work, incorporated vendor terms, and a data-processing addendum when the facts require one. State document precedence expressly, including which document governs license restrictions versus your own service obligations. Scope must identify SKU, quantity, tenant, authorized users, subscription period, support tier, migration assumptions, and exclusions. Define the fee trigger separately for license delivery and services: an accepted private offer may create a payment commitment before an implementation milestone is accepted. A hypothetical $24,000 implementation package with $14,400 direct delivery cost leaves $9,600 contribution before overhead; it does not establish a 40% enterprise net margin. Use testable acceptance criteria such as twenty designated users completing SSO login and an agreed migration sample passing reconciliation. Give the customer a defined review period, a written defect process, and a correction path. Do not make a vendor's entire product roadmap your deliverable. Change orders must price additional connectors, historical data cleanup, and customer-caused delays before contractors perform the extra work. Where an automatic acceptance mechanism is used, make notice and review rights explicit and assess enforceability under the governing law.

Allocate liability to the actor that controls the risk. A negotiated cap might reference fees paid or payable under the affected order during twelve months, but that is a bargaining position, not a universally enforceable formula. Define treatment of confidentiality, security incidents, IP indemnities, intentional misconduct, and unpaid fees without casually accepting unlimited exposure for every breach. Check whether vendor remedies actually flow through to your buyer; a vendor's liability cap does not automatically cap your independent promises. Specify indemnity notice, defense control, settlement consent, and exclusions for customer modifications or combinations. Separate customer data, preexisting reseller tools, vendor software, and bespoke deliverables in the ownership clause. Give the customer sufficient rights to use paid deliverables while retaining reusable methods where negotiated. Choose governing law, forum, escalation contacts, and a dispute process that preserves practical collection options. Review mandatory venue, sovereign-immunity, and arbitration restrictions for public customers. UCC Article 2 applicability varies with state law and the software-service mix; draft payment and acceptance mechanics explicitly rather than assuming one classification settles every remedy. Contract terms should explain suspension and data retrieval, not permit surprise lockouts of unrelated customer systems.

Keep the canonical annual model separate from illustrative order spreads. Conservative billings of $300,000 at 8% leave $24,000 owner net profit and imply $276,000 total costs. Base billings of $1,400,000 at 14.0% leave $196,000 and imply $1,204,000 costs. Scaled billings of $2,500,000 at 20% leave $500,000 and imply $2,000,000 costs. Vendor costs are already inside these totals; subtracting them again would understate profit. Conservative and Base each use two full-time staff plus three contractors; Scaled uses three full-time staff plus four contractors. Renewal management on a hypothetical $200,000 renewal at a 12% initial spread produces $24,000 before overhead, not another annual profit scenario. License reconciliation that identifies forty unused $30 monthly seats identifies $14,400 annual customer spend, not reseller revenue. Bill a separately agreed $3,000 review fee only when its stated deliverable is accepted. For slow collections, a $100,000 vendor payment preceding customer receipt by sixty days ties up $100,000; at an illustrative 12% annual carrying rate, that interval costs about $1,973. Deposits, credit limits, and enforceable suspension rights are commercial controls, not substitutes for cash forecasting.

sections.heading: 3. Apply state, sector, and procurement rules to the actual delivery model
paragraphs: Data-processing duties follow what the reseller actually does. A license-only seller that never accesses customer records differs from an implementer migrating employee files or administering production tenants. Map collection, access, storage, support exports, subprocessors, retention, and deletion before assigning contract roles. California Civil Code § 1798.100 requires specified contractual treatment for covered disclosures; service-provider and contractor restrictions also depend on the applicable definitions and regulations. Do not assume every business customer or every reseller falls within the same scope. Other state privacy laws use different thresholds, exemptions, and processor duties. Attach the appropriate addendum when facts establish coverage, and prohibit using implementation records for unrelated marketing. In healthcare, receiving or maintaining protected health information on behalf of a covered entity can create business-associate duties under HIPAA. A vendor's BAA does not cover your separate consulting company merely because both touch the same tenant. Apply least privilege through Microsoft Entra or the relevant cloud IAM system, with named accounts and time-bounded access. Keep production credentials out of CRM notes. Use synthetic discovery data until the processing arrangement and access controls are established. Specify incident notice timing contractually while preserving applicable statutory deadlines.

Separate customer security questionnaires from statutory applicability and procurement authority. A bank may impose vendor-management and incident-reporting terms that exceed the reseller's direct obligations; evaluate those promises before signing. Schools can require FERPA-compatible access restrictions and state student-data terms. Public-sector orders add purchasing authority, funding, competition, and recordkeeping questions that commercial templates do not answer. FAR 12.212 addresses federal acquisition of commercial computer software and documentation; it does not authorize a salesperson to accept agency-specific deviations or prove that a contracting officer has funds. Identify the actual purchasing vehicle, authorized buyer, applicable clauses, and order precedence. Never describe a product as government-authorized, domestically sourced, or security-certified without evidence matching the claim's scope. Knowingly false material certifications can create exposure under 31 U.S.C. § 3729. For an illustrative $150,000 public-sector order with $126,000 vendor cost, $24,000 initial spread must absorb bid preparation, required reporting, and delivery costs. If the vehicle does not permit the reseller or product, use a properly authorized prime relationship rather than borrowing another company's contract number. Document subcontract compensation and responsibilities before treating the opportunity as executable revenue.

Create a state-by-state issue register around customer location, delivery location, transaction type, and contract term. Software taxability can change between downloaded software, remote access, maintenance, and separately stated implementation. Economic nexus and resale-certificate rules also vary; a marketplace's collection activity does not automatically settle every direct-sale obligation. Use the relevant state revenue department's classifications, supported by transaction facts, rather than copying a distributor's tax result. An illustrative 6% tax on a taxable $50,000 order is $3,000 collected for remittance, not additional operator revenue. Automatic-renewal requirements vary by state and by business versus consumer customer; New York General Obligations Law § 5-903 can affect certain service, maintenance, or repair contracts when its conditions apply. Check scope and required notice timing instead of assuming all enterprise subscriptions are exempt. State breach-notification statutes require a separate assessment from privacy-law applicability. Maintain a renewal calendar keyed to statutory notice, contractual cancellation, and vendor commitment deadlines. If notice was missed, determine the actual remedy before asserting that the customer owes another year. Preserve approved notice text, recipient records, and delivery evidence with the renewal order.

sections.heading: 4. Use evidence-backed outreach and bound the payment-orchestration adjacency
paragraphs: Commercial email to business recipients remains subject to CAN-SPAM, including accurate routing information, nondeceptive subjects, applicable advertising identification, a valid postal address, and a working opt-out honored within ten business days. Do not harvest addresses through unauthorized access or buy lists without reviewing provenance and suppression handling. Telephone and text campaigns require a separate TCPA, FCC, and state-law analysis based on technology, number type, purpose, and required permission; a business title is not universal permission to text a personal mobile. Use this email body: 'I work with enterprise buyers on license reconciliation and authorized renewal options. Would a review of your next renewal's seat count, term, and implementation requirements be useful? I would first confirm whether our vendor authorization covers your product and purchasing entity. This is a commercial inquiry. Reply stop to end outreach.' Append the actual sender identity, monitored reply address, and valid postal address before sending. In discovery say: 'Who owns the subscription, which entity signs, what cancellation deadline applies, and may we review a redacted entitlement export?' Do not request passwords, assert savings without a baseline, or imply vendor endorsement beyond documented rights.

The supplied adjacent play high_risk_payfac_iso_mid_cascading_arbitrage concerns wholesale high-risk ISO and payment-orchestration economics, not an ordinary software-reseller license. Its proposed 25–60 domestic and offshore acquiring relationships require genuine bank approval, applicable network registration, underwriting, and jurisdiction-specific review. Vertical labels such as telehealth GLP-1 products, peptides, nutraceutical subscriptions, sweepstakes gaming, coaching, and AI companions do not establish lawful merchandise or acquirer eligibility. A prohibition by Stripe or PayPal is not permission to conceal the merchant elsewhere. On $100,000 merchant processing volume, a 2.10% buy rate costs $2,100 and a 5.50%–8.90% sell rate generates $5,500–$8,900 processing charges, leaving $3,400–$6,800 before other fees, losses, and operating costs. Merchant volume is not reseller revenue, and an ISO may recognize only its contractual residual. A 10% rolling reserve holds $10,000 for the stated release schedule; it is neither earned spread nor available operating cash. Do not add these adjacent figures to the volume's canonical annual cases. Selling integration software does not authorize custody of funds, merchant aggregation, or use of another business's merchant identifier. Funds flow determines whether additional payments licensing analysis is required.

For that adjacent play, define cascading narrowly as routing permitted transactions among disclosed, approved acquiring relationships under applicable network and bank rules. Never retry to defeat an issuer restriction, conceal a merchant, misstate a descriptor, or bypass a prohibited-business decision. The risk fallback is a contractually required 10% rolling reserve for accepted merchants, automated Verifi Rapid Dispute Resolution refunds where eligible and configured, supported 3DS2 step-up authentication using approved risk signals, and strict descriptor transparency. These measures do not cure illegal sales or guarantee authorization. If a bank rejects the activity, disable the route and return the case for underwriting rather than silently moving volume offshore. Say: 'We implement orchestration only for merchant entities and activities approved by your acquiring partners. Please provide the approved entity, descriptor, permitted products, routing restrictions, and reserve schedule before technical discovery.' Price a bounded $12,000 integration against $7,200 direct implementation cost for $4,800 contribution before overhead, with payment credentials tokenized through approved providers. The safer fallback is software-only implementation or a disclosed referral with explicit compensation, no fund custody, and no promise of acquiring acceptance. Suspend work when evidence contradicts the merchant's stated activity.

chapters.question_prompt: How does a 2 FT + 3 C (5 people) enterprise software reselling team automate 70%+ of repetitive research, qualification, fulfillment, and traffic/deal acquisition while keeping human-in-the-loop QA?
chapters.title: Automation, AI Leverage & Scalable Distribution Flywheels
chapters.subtitle: Python Event Pipelines, AWS CPPO and Microsoft CSP Workflows, Renewal Intelligence, and Human-Controlled Quote Economics
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #23, Enterprise Software Reselling, holds Rank #14 with a 87/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Its leverage comes from automating evidence movement, not delegating commercial authority to a model. This chapter connects nine mapped plays: account research, qualification, deal registration, quote preparation, marketplace offers, implementation attachment, license reconciliation, renewal orchestration, and distribution referrals. A 2 FT + 3 C pod uses Python workers, signed webhooks, constrained LLM extraction, and named human reviewers to target 70%+ removal of repetitive labor. Canonical annual owner profits remain $24,000 Conservative, $196,000 Base, and $500,000 Scaled; the Scaled case requires 3 FT + 4 C. Instrument run costs, authorization evidence, collections, and recovery paths before expanding automated volume.

sections.heading: 1. Map nine operator plays into one evidence-controlled event system
paragraphs: Build the automation boundary around a commercial record, not around an autonomous salesperson. Candidate #23's nine mapped operator plays are account research, qualification, deal registration, quote preparation, marketplace offer execution, implementation attachment, license reconciliation, renewal orchestration, and distribution referrals. Treat this chapter's mapping as the operating taxonomy, with one accountable owner and one measurable output per play. The first full-time operator owns vendor relationships, pricing decisions, procurement conversations, and customer commitments. The second owns delivery coordination, renewal operations, collections visibility, and exception triage. Three contractors supply bounded integration engineering, implementation capacity, and channel content production; contractor seats do not imply unlimited weekly hours. Record each person's contracted availability before allocating review work. HubSpot or Salesforce holds the opportunity record; a PostgreSQL event ledger holds processing history; vendor portals remain authoritative for program rights and transaction status. Assign stable customer, tenant, opportunity, and subscription identifiers before adding AI. Similar company names, subsidiaries, and shared email domains otherwise produce attractive but incorrect account matches. Every event must carry its source, retrieval time, permission scope, and evidence link so a reviewer can reconstruct the decision without searching chat transcripts. Separate customer-specific records from reusable channel templates at ingestion, rather than trusting a later prompt to separate them.

Use Python 3.9 workers for normalization, deterministic arithmetic, and workflow routing; use an LLM only where extraction or drafting beats a fixed parser. A webhook receiver verifies the provider's supported signature or authentication mechanism, checks freshness where supported, persists the event durably, and acknowledges receipt before expensive processing. AWS API Gateway, Lambda, and SQS provide one implementation; an authenticated service and managed queue provide another. The ledger stores event_id, source, account_id, object_version, payload_hash, received_at, state, and reviewer_id. Enforce a unique source-event key to neutralize retries. Workers fetch current authoritative records before preparing consequential changes because delivery can be duplicated or out of order. Put credentials in AWS Secrets Manager or Azure Key Vault, grant separate read and write identities, and redact tokens from traces. Documents, email bodies, and web pages are untrusted evidence: instructions inside them cannot authorize tools, change pricing rules, or select another customer's records. Send the model only the fields required for the current task. Persist structured output separately from source evidence, validate its schema, and route unsupported claims to a reviewer rather than allowing persuasive prose to fill missing facts. Tenant isolation must be enforced by application queries and storage permissions, not by the model's willingness to obey a prompt.

Measure the 70% target as avoided repetitive labor on a fixed workload, not as the percentage of messages touched by software. Establish a two-week baseline across research, qualification, fulfillment preparation, and acquisition operations, recording active minutes and completed outcomes. In an illustrative matched cohort of 100 events, manual handling consumes 1,000 minutes. After automation, scheduled human review consumes 220 minutes and exception recovery consumes 60 minutes, leaving 280 minutes and removing 72% of repetitive effort. This is a measurement design, not a forecast for every reseller. Include rework, sampling, queue maintenance, and failed runs in the automated cohort; otherwise the dashboard conceals labor in contractors' inboxes. Break results out by play because an easy research classifier can mask a fragile provisioning workflow. Track unsupported-claim rate, quote correction rate, entitlement mismatch rate, and time to resolve exceptions alongside minutes saved. Reserve named review windows for the two full-time operators and cap releases at their actual capacity. When the queue exceeds that cap, slow intake instead of relaxing evidence requirements. The target concerns repetitive handling; negotiation, vendor disputes, architecture choices, and customer commitments remain human work. Publish a weekly denominator showing eligible events, excluded events, and the reason for each exclusion.

sections.heading: 2. Automate renewals, quote preparation, and license reconciliation safely
paragraphs: Start renewal orchestration with signed order terms and current subscription records, not with a universal ninety-day countdown. Microsoft CSP new commerce subscriptions can have term-specific change and cancellation rules; AWS Marketplace agreements and private offers carry their own commercial conditions. Store term end, renewal behavior, notice deadline, quantity, billing cadence, and the source supporting each field. A daily Python scheduler computes configurable reminders at 120, 90, 60, and 30 days where those dates are useful, then prioritizes the earliest binding action deadline. A model may extract candidate dates from an order document, but deterministic date checks and a reviewer must establish the operative record. Compare purchased seats with assigned and meaningfully used seats only where customer authorization covers those datasets. Generate a renewal packet containing the current entitlement snapshot, unresolved support issues, proposed scope, and quote assumptions. Suppress duplicate messages after a customer response and keep an audit trail of delivery failures. Never let an inferred usage decline trigger automatic cancellation, employee deprovisioning, or seat reduction. Those actions can interrupt operations and may not reduce the current contractual obligation. Escalate approaching deadlines to the relationship owner with a specific decision request and a documented last-safe action time.

Quote generation should resemble a compiler: approved inputs enter, reproducible commercial outputs leave, and invalid combinations fail visibly. Represent currency with Python Decimal, store the currency code explicitly, and distinguish monthly billing from the full committed term. Validate SKU, region, customer segment, license metric, support tier, quantity, term dates, tax treatment, and vendor authorization before rendering a document. Keep vendor acquisition cost, customer license price, implementation price, marketplace charges, and expected delivery cost in separate fields. An LLM can draft the scope narrative from approved facts; it cannot invent discounts, service levels, indemnities, or eligibility. AWS Channel Partner Private Offers use applicable selling authorizations and reseller offer mechanics; Microsoft CSP ordering follows the partner's actual direct or indirect relationship and supported Partner Center capabilities. Do not assume equivalent APIs or pricing controls across those routes. Persist a quote version and its input digest, then require the commercial owner to approve the exact rendered output before customer release. If vendor pricing changes, expire the draft and regenerate it rather than silently modifying a reviewed quote. Customer acceptance must link to the accepted version, not merely to the opportunity's latest document. This prevents later reconciliation from treating an unsigned revision as contractual evidence.

License reconciliation joins three different truths: contractual entitlement, provisioning state, and observed assignment. Collect authorized exports through Microsoft Graph, Partner Center, vendor APIs, or customer-provided files according to available permissions; access to one system does not imply permission to inspect every tenant. Normalize timestamps, SKU aliases, tenant identifiers, subscription identifiers, and effective dates before comparing quantities. Shared devices, pooled licenses, service accounts, and bundle components require product-specific rules, not a universal named-user calculation. Classify differences as timing lag, mapping error, assignment exception, or commercial discrepancy, with evidence attached to each finding. A reconciliation result creates a remediation proposal, never an automatic accusation or purchase. For fulfillment, use a state machine such as prepared, reviewed, submitted, confirmed, and exception. Before retrying an ambiguous submission, query the provider's transaction record; a timeout after acceptance must not create duplicate purchases. Use provider idempotency features where supported and maintain local duplicate protection regardless. Reversible internal updates can be retried automatically, while purchases and access changes require stronger confirmation. If the API is unavailable, export a dated review packet for a designated operator to process through the authorized portal, then reconcile the portal receipt into the ledger before resuming automated writes.

sections.heading: 3. Build distribution loops from verified deployment evidence
paragraphs: Programmatic distribution should publish useful procurement and deployment knowledge, not thousands of lightly rewritten product pages. Build a controlled catalog of vendor-approved product facts, deployment prerequisites, supported procurement routes, implementation scope patterns, and dated pricing assumptions. A Python generator can assemble segment-specific pages for a narrow workload, such as Microsoft 365 tenant consolidation or a documented AWS Marketplace purchasing path, while an LLM drafts readable explanations from that catalog. Each page needs an actual operator contribution: a migration checklist, entitlement worksheet, private offer readiness assessment, or implementation acceptance template. Do not imply vendor endorsement, reproduce restricted partner material, or publish customer-derived configurations without the required rights. Under 17 U.S.C. 106, reproduction and adaptation rights matter even when a model rewrites source material. Store publication permissions beside reusable assets, and review brand-use conditions separately. Instrument Search Console, first-party form submissions, and CRM attribution to measure qualified opportunities rather than raw page count. Version pages when vendor terms change and remove obsolete transaction instructions promptly. Publication remains a human-reviewed external action; internal drafts can be generated freely within the authorized source boundary. A smaller library of accurate, maintained assets is easier for a five-person pod to defend and convert.

Outbound automation should improve account selection and evidence quality before it increases message volume. Use authorized account lists and documented firmographic sources to identify companies with a plausible deployment need, then draft a short hypothesis tied to public facts. Do not present inferred software usage, renewal dates, or buying authority as confirmed information. The relationship owner reviews targeting rules and initial sequences; routine messages may run only within the approved campaign scope and suppression controls. For commercial email, 15 U.S.C. 7704 supplies concrete requirements covering truthful transmission information, nondeceptive subjects, required identification, a valid physical postal address, and a functioning opt-out mechanism. Honor applicable opt-outs within ten business days and suppress internally immediately when received. Keep a durable suppression record that survives list refreshes. Stop sequences on replies, complaints, and delivery failures; do not route around provider restrictions with replacement identities. Qualification automation can summarize responses and propose discovery questions, but pricing promises and vendor eligibility claims require verified evidence. Track positive replies, accepted meetings, qualified opportunities, paid invoices, and delivery contribution as separate stages. A campaign producing many meetings but expensive unqualified implementation requests is consuming scarce pod capacity rather than creating a distribution advantage. Feed that result back into targeting rules each week.

The strongest referral loop begins after a verified operational win. Following an authorized license cleanup or successful implementation, prepare a customer-facing evidence pack showing the starting condition, approved changes, measured outcome, and remaining tasks. Ask the customer whether they want a version suitable for an internal purchasing committee or a peer introduction; do not assume permission to name their organization publicly. Reusable worksheets and readiness assessments can circulate among procurement, IT, and department leaders, bringing the reseller into additional buying conversations without revealing tenant-level data. Attribute introductions with explicit CRM relationship records rather than hidden tracking. Separately, use permitted vendor co-selling and deal-registration processes to return high-quality opportunity evidence to the channel manager. Accurate scope, clean buyer identity, and dependable implementation follow-through make the next referral easier to evaluate. Route new leads back through the same qualification and authorization checks; referral status does not establish purchasing authority. Measure the loop as collected contribution from referred accounts divided by the fully loaded effort required to support it. Feed objections and delivery defects into the content catalog, then update the corresponding research and quote templates. This creates compounding operating knowledge without pretending that traffic, partner introductions, or marketplace visibility automatically become recognized revenue.

sections.heading: 4. Price automation, rehearse recovery, and scale only measured capacity
paragraphs: Price every automated run with explicit assumptions and include the human work it creates. For an illustrative extraction task, assume 1,500 input tokens at $2 per million and 500 output tokens at $8 per million: model cost is $0.003 plus $0.004, or $0.007. Add an assumed $0.005 for queue, compute, logging, and attributable storage, producing $0.012 of machine cost per completed run. These are planning inputs, not quoted provider prices. If 20% of runs receive three minutes of review at a loaded $60 hourly rate, expected review cost is $0.60 per run and combined cost is $0.612. At 5,000 runs monthly, that means $60 machine expense plus $3,000 review expense, with 50 review hours required. Add exception investigation, software subscriptions, and maintenance separately; the example does not conceal them inside token pricing. High-consequence quotes and purchasing actions still receive complete review, so this sampling assumption applies only to the eligible low-risk extraction population. Estimate each play separately and set budget alarms on actual retries and model usage. Cheap text generation can still be operationally expensive when weak extraction pushes hundreds of ambiguous records into the two full-time operators' queues. The earlier labor-saving cohort is a separate experiment, not this cost model's denominator.

Keep the canonical scorecard intact when evaluating these costs. Conservative gross license resale and service billings are $300,000; an 8% net margin leaves $24,000 annual owner net profit and implies $276,000 of total modeled costs. Base billings of $1,400,000 at 14.0% leave $196,000 and imply $1,204,000 of costs. Scaled billings of $2,500,000 at 20% leave $500,000 and imply $2,000,000 of costs. Vendor acquisition costs are included within those margins, not deducted again from the stated profits. Conservative and Base use 2 FT + 3 C; Scaled uses 3 FT + 4 C, seven people rather than five. Allocate automation expense within the relevant modeled cost envelope or explicitly revise an implementation budget; never add hypothetical labor savings directly to canonical owner profit. Keep customer cloud consumption and unrelated marketplace spend outside reseller billings. Where a particular arrangement makes the business an agent, determine the applicable presentation rather than assuming every routed dollar is gross revenue; this chapter preserves the supplied gross-resale scorecard basis. Track implementation scope contribution separately from license resale contribution, then reconcile both with shared operating costs. Slow customer collections can still create a cash shortfall when vendor obligations fall due before customer receipts.

Scale by proving repeatability under failure, not by removing the last reviewer. Maintain test fixtures for duplicate webhooks, expired vendor authorization, mismatched tenants, changed prices, rejected model output, ambiguous purchase responses, and delayed customer payment. Rehearse queue replay with writes disabled, then compare proposed actions against recorded outcomes before permitting production execution. Use bounded exponential backoff with jitter for transient errors, stop retries on permission failures, and send exhausted events to an owned exception queue. A nightly reconciliation should detect events that never reached a terminal state and compare external receipts with internal commitments. Restrict emergency access and record every manual portal action. Under 18 U.S.C. 1030, automation does not create authorization to access systems beyond granted scope. For covered federal contract information systems, implement FAR 52.204-21 when the clause applies, including required access controls and safeguarding practices. Assign the integration contractor a documented restoration procedure and train a full-time operator to use it. Before moving toward the seven-person Scaled configuration, verify review capacity, collected contribution, defect rates, and support coverage over several complete renewal and delivery cycles. More events are useful only when the pod can preserve evidence, fulfill commitments, and recover without turning vendor-policy changes into customer-facing errors.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #23, Enterprise Software Reselling, ranks #14 with a 87/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. Its nine mapped operator plays become transferable assets only when authorization, deal registration, CPPO, CSP, quoting, implementation, license reconciliation, renewals, and collections have named owners and auditable handoffs. Start with 2 FT + 3 C; add one employee and one contractor only against measured workload and collected contribution. Canonical annual owner profits are $24,000 Conservative, $196,000 Base, and $500,000 Scaled. Protect those economics with milestone-based contractor compensation, weekly exception reviews, customer and counterparty concentration limits of 25%, cohort accounting, and signed intellectual-property assignments. Build the same evidence whether selling or retaining the company: renewable gross profit, replaceable owner labor, transferable agreements, and cash collections that survive vendor policy changes.

sections.heading: 1. Assign Nine Plays to Five Seats Before Expanding to Seven
paragraphs: Build the starting pod around two accountable employees and three bounded contractor engagements, not five interchangeable generalists. For this chapter, the nine-play execution map is P1 reseller authorization, P2 deal registration, P3 AWS Marketplace channel partner private offers, P4 Microsoft CSP subscription operations, P5 quote generation, P6 implementation delivery, P7 license reconciliation, P8 renewal management, and P9 collections. FT1 is the owner-led commercial principal: they own P1, P2, pricing exceptions, vendor relationships, and material customer commitments. FT2 is the revenue-operations and customer success lead: they own P4, P5, P7, P8, and the collections queue under P9. Contractor C1 supplies certified solution architecture for P3 and technical scoping; C2 delivers P6 through accepted milestones; C3 maintains the accrual ledger and collection evidence supporting P9. No contractor independently changes payment instructions, reseller eligibility, or contract commitments. Use a HubSpot company record as the commercial index, Jira Service Management for delivery evidence, and QuickBooks Online or an equivalent accrual ledger for accounting. Store the vendor account identifier, customer tenant identifier, contract identifier, and renewal anniversary on every opportunity. Those identifiers connect all nine plays without making the founder the only person who can reconstruct a transaction.

Separate ownership from execution so that absence does not become a service failure. FT1 approves a quote's commercial spread, while FT2 verifies the customer entity, quantity, term, billing frequency, and underlying authorization. C1 documents architecture assumptions before C2 commits implementation hours; C2 returns test evidence before FT2 marks delivery accepted. C3 reconciles the customer receivable, distributor payable, marketplace settlement, and bank receipt without possessing unilateral bank-release authority. Keep approval evidence in the deal record rather than an employee's mailbox. For AWS CPPO, record the selling authorization, permitted offer economics, expiration, and applicable seller-of-record arrangement; do not assume Microsoft CSP has the same money flow or transfer rules. In CSP, identify whether the business is an indirect reseller or direct-bill partner and which party owns provisioning, support, billing, and cancellation obligations. Escalate conflicting portal data before sending the customer an executable quote. Maintain two individually assigned administrators with least-privilege access and tested recovery procedures; never solve continuity by sharing credentials. A weekly absence drill should let the backup operator locate the signed order, accepted scope, next renewal action, and outstanding receivable within ten minutes. Record failures as specific missing artifacts and close them before another customer enters the same workflow.

Expand to three employees and four contractors only when workload, service quality, and cash support the added capacity. The third employee becomes the dedicated renewals and customer-success manager, taking P8 and routine P7 follow-up from FT2. The fourth contractor supplies independently scoped integration or testing capacity for P6, rather than becoming an uncounted permanent support desk. Use a four-week trigger: more than thirty accepted renewal actions waiting beyond two business days, or implementation commitments exceeding eighty percent of contracted delivery capacity, combined with adequate cash for the signed vendor obligations and the incremental staffing commitment. These are operating triggers, not additions to the canonical profit forecast. The Conservative case still has two full-time seats and three contractors; its $24,000 annual owner profit leaves little room for rework, recruiting errors, or richer compensation. Model actual wages, payroll burden, contractor hours, and owner duties before treating that case as a viable launch budget. Full-time seats are real work commitments, not permission to omit labor costs. Contractor engagements need defined outputs and genuine independence; labels alone do not determine worker status. Review federal tax classification under 26 U.S.C. section 3121(d), applicable wage rules, and relevant state tests before establishing recurring arrangements.

callout.title: Make Vendor Knowledge Portable Before the Founder Takes Leave
callout.body: The valuable asset is the documented operating relationship, not a founder's memory of which channel manager answers quickly.
items: Attach the actual CPPO selling authorization and offer expiration to the deal record; a saved price screenshot does not establish continuing resale rights.
Export CSP subscription identifiers and scheduled renewal changes into the operating register before staff changes; portal access alone does not explain customer intent.
Require C1 to document the rejected architecture alternative and its cost consequence, making replacement scoping faster and preventing repeated presales labor.
Run one founder-absent renewal every month using named backup operators, then repair the missing permissions, contract evidence, or customer introductions it exposes.

sections.heading: 2. Buy Accepted Contractor Outputs and Run a Weekly Exception Scorecard
paragraphs: Compensate contractors for defined deliverables while retaining a transparent view of effective hourly cost. An illustrative architecture statement of work pays $1,200 for discovery, a written design, a license bill of materials, and one revision within an agreed scope. An illustrative implementation engagement pays $4,800 against three accepted milestones: twenty percent for the tested plan, fifty percent for configured staging and test evidence, and thirty percent for production acceptance and handover. Those amounts illustrate procurement mechanics; they do not replace the scorecard's expense envelope. The agreement must define the customer inputs, review window, objective acceptance tests, change pricing, and payment deadline. Pay undisputed accepted work on time, and separate a specific defect dispute from unrelated invoices. Use a five-business-day review window and document whether acceptance was granted or which contracted criterion failed. For architect scoping errors or implementation defects within the original scope, specify a correction obligation with an agreed response target. Do not make the contractor insure vendor outages, customer scope changes, or disputed sales promises. Track rework hours against the responsible cause so a seemingly cheap contractor cannot hide costs inside FT2's workload or the owner's unrecorded nights and weekends.

Set service levels around business consequences rather than demanding constant availability from every contractor. A critical production defect requires acknowledgment within four contracted coverage hours, an incident owner, and a restoration plan; restoration time remains dependent on the failure and the agreed scope. A standard quote should reach internal review within two business days after complete inputs arrive. License reconciliation exceptions should have an owner within one business day and a documented resolution or vendor escalation within five. Define coverage calendars, time zones, escalation contacts, and customer dependencies explicitly. Measure first-pass acceptance as deliverables accepted without contractor-caused correction divided by deliverables reviewed; target at least ninety-five percent over a rolling quarter, displaying the denominator beside the percentage. Require every contractor creating code, scripts, templates, or documentation to sign an assignment covering the commissioned deliverables. Under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a), a copyright ownership transfer generally requires a writing signed by the owner or their authorized agent. Do not assume paying an invoice transfers copyright. Identify background tools, third-party components, and customer-owned materials separately, with sufficient licenses for continued operation and a permitted business transfer. Collect assignments before delivery begins and reconcile them to the repository and acceptance record at closeout.

Run a forty-five-minute Monday scorecard using a locked Friday snapshot. FT2 publishes the dataset; FT1 chairs exception decisions; contractors attend only the portions covered by their engagements. Start with cash: overdue receivables, vendor payments due within thirty days, disputed settlements, and contribution remaining after direct vendor and contractor costs. Then inspect renewal coverage at 120, 90, 60, and 30 days, quote cycle time, first-pass implementation acceptance, and unmatched licenses. Finish with concentration and missing transfer evidence. Never reward total license billings alone: a large discounted renewal can increase revenue while reducing cash and owner profit. Define gross-profit retention on a fixed opening renewal cohort, using retained gross profit before expansion; report expansion separately so a large new tenant cannot disguise customer losses. Measure days sales outstanding on the same gross or net accounting basis as the underlying receivable and credit sales. Assign each exception one owner, one next action, one deadline, and one economic exposure. Carry unresolved items forward visibly rather than rebuilding a cleaner-looking list. A red metric triggers an intervention, such as shortening credit terms or revising a scope template, not an automatic contractor penalty unsupported by the signed agreement.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile Accrual Cohorts and Cap Every Material Dependency
paragraphs: Anchor the ledger to the canonical scenarios before adding operational detail. Conservative gross revenue is $300,000, with an eight percent net margin and $24,000 annual owner net profit; the implied total cost envelope is $276,000. Base gross revenue is $1,400,000, with a fourteen percent net margin and $196,000 owner net profit; the implied costs are $1,204,000. Scaled gross revenue is $2,500,000, with a twenty percent net margin and $500,000 owner net profit; the implied costs are $2,000,000. Vendor license costs sit inside those envelopes, together with delivery, labor, overhead, and other modeled expenses. Do not treat these gross billings as a commission-only revenue stream, and do not add a customer's wider cloud consumption or software estate to operator revenue. The scorecard uses gross license resale and service billings; actual reporting requires a contract-specific principal-versus-agent assessment under the applicable accounting framework. If a particular offer belongs on a net presentation, show a separate reconciliation rather than silently changing the canonical case. Keep customer cash advances, earned service revenue, vendor obligations, and marketplace receivables distinct. A bank balance boosted by prepaid subscriptions is not automatically distributable owner cash, especially when the related supplier payment or delivery obligation remains outstanding.

Close each month by contract, customer, vendor, and renewal cohort. Preserve original booking date, service period, invoice date, cash date, vendor cost, marketplace deductions, implementation cost, and the evidence supporting recognition. Recognize implementation work according to the applicable performance obligations, not merely because C2 submitted an invoice. Record customer prepayments as liabilities until the relevant recognition conditions are met; record unpaid earned amounts and supplier accruals consistently. Match credits, cancellations, incentives, and disputed rebates to their originating contracts so a cleanup month does not appear to be a sudden margin collapse. Treat contingent vendor incentives separately until their contractual and accounting conditions are satisfied. For renewal analysis, freeze the opening customer cohort and calculate retained license gross profit, lost gross profit, pricing changes, and incremental implementation contribution as separate bridges. A $100,000 license invoice with $88,000 vendor cost creates $12,000 before delivery and overhead, not $100,000 of recurring contribution. If a related implementation sells for $15,000 and consumes $9,000 of direct delivery cost, its $6,000 contribution is a distinct service spread. These illustrative units explain the ledger; they are not additional revenue assumed in any canonical scenario. Reconcile all cohort totals back to the closed general ledger before circulating them to lenders, prospective buyers, or the operating team.

Set a twenty-five percent maximum for any customer or common-control customer group on both trailing-twelve-month revenue and gross profit. Apply the same maximum to material independent counterparty dependencies: vendor-attributable gross profit, distributor purchase obligations, and marketplace settlement receivables. Calculate each category separately; averaging them conceals a single point of failure. Vendor groups under common control belong together, and two distributors selling the same indispensable publisher do not eliminate publisher risk. A young specialist may initially exceed a cap because the first few customers or one platform dominate. Report the actual breach, freeze discretionary increases in that dependency where commercially feasible, and assign a dated diversification plan rather than declaring the business diversified. Maintain existing contractual service commitments while redirecting new acquisition. Distinguish concentration from absolute cash exposure: a small overdue marketplace balance can threaten payroll even when its percentage looks acceptable. Stress-test a sixty-day collection delay, loss of the largest renewable gross-profit account, and a vendor discount reduction against signed payables and staffing commitments. Use those tests to size cash reserves and credit terms; do not quietly reduce the stated profit cases. A buyer should see historical breaches, corrective actions, and current exposure, not a chart that removes inconvenient accounts from the denominator.

sections.heading: 4. Price Transferable Earnings, Then Choose an Exit or Durable Distributions
paragraphs: Value the business on transferable earnings rather than the face value of licenses passing through it. For initial negotiation planning, an owner-operated small reseller might be tested at two to three times verified seller's discretionary earnings; a more transferable operation with defensible recurring gross profit might justify testing three to four times. Treat these as illustrative screening bands, not observed transaction comparables or an entitlement. A strategic buyer may instead price adjusted EBITDA, customer contribution, or a portfolio of transferable renewals. Do not multiply the $196,000 Base owner net profit by an EBITDA multiple without reconciling the earnings definitions. Build the bridge from the closed ledger: identify owner compensation already expensed, genuine nonrecurring items, interest, depreciation, taxes under the chosen metric, and the recurring cost of replacing necessary owner work. Include contractor normalization if historical delivery depended on discounted introductory rates. For an owner-operator buyer, SDE typically adds back one working owner's compensation; for a manager-run valuation, replacement leadership cost remains a real expense. Explain which buyer and operating model each bridge serves. A documented renewal engine can support stronger pricing, but it cannot convert cancellable vendor permissions into perpetual assets or erase a concentration breach that threatens future contribution.

Use explicit assumptions when translating a screening multiple into dollars. If diligence establishes that normalized SDE equals the Base case's $196,000 owner profit, a two-to-three-times range produces $392,000 to $588,000 of illustrative enterprise value. That equality is an assumption to verify, not an accounting identity. If the Scaled operation's $500,000 owner profit likewise equals verified SDE and its transfer evidence supports the stronger three-to-four-times screening band, the illustrative enterprise value is $1,500,000 to $2,000,000. Do not present either range as proceeds available at closing. Bridge enterprise value to equity proceeds using the agreed treatment of cash, debt, debt-like obligations, transaction expenses, escrow, and normalized working capital. Define whether distributor payables and customer prepayments belong in working capital or another purchase-price category, and prevent double counting. A renewal earnout should specify the opening cohort, measurement period, gross-profit definition, collection requirements, permitted pricing changes, and buyer obligations that affect retention. Prefer measures the seller can inspect over an unrestricted buyer-wide profit metric. Test how vendor repricing, customer cancellation, and delayed marketplace settlements change the payout before agreeing to a headline price that depends heavily on future contingent consideration.

Build the transfer room while operating, not after signing an exclusive sale process. Index customer contracts, reseller and distributor agreements, authorization histories, renewal cohorts, signed assignments, delivery acceptance, incident history, employee responsibilities, and contractor replacement plans. Keep commercial diligence separate from production access: share redacted evidence under an executed confidentiality agreement and restrict customer data to the diligence purpose. Identify which contracts require assignment consent or notice and which vendor programs require fresh partner qualification. Selling shares does not automatically bypass change-of-control provisions. For United States federal contracts, examine 41 U.S.C. section 6305 and FAR 42.1204 when evaluating whether recognition of a successor requires novation; do not assume commercial customer assignment rules apply. If retaining the company, use the same evidence to run a durable distribution policy: close the ledger, fund taxes and signed obligations, reserve for collection delays and delivery commitments, then distribute genuinely available cash. Review owner hours quarterly and charge replacement labor in the internal operating model even when the owner performs the work. The strongest cash cow and the strongest sale candidate share one characteristic: customers renew because the pod reliably delivers and reconciles value, not because the founder personally rescues every quote, invoice, implementation, and renewal.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #23, Enterprise Software Reselling, ranks #14 with a 87/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This sprint organizes nine mapped plays around authorized resale, deal registration, AWS CPPO, Microsoft CSP, license reconciliation, implementation, migration, support, and renewals. The first thirty days establish an executable channel, documented buyer demand, priced delivery capacity, and a protected cash position; they do not compress a three-to-twelve-month first-deal cycle into four weeks. A 2 FT + 3 C pod advances through daily deliverables and explicit Day 30/60/90 decisions. Canonical annual owner profit remains $24,000 Conservative, $196,000 Base, and $500,000 Scaled. Expand only the motion whose authorization, buyer evidence, contribution economics, and settlement timing survive inspection; terminate invalid routes before adding commitments.

sections.heading: 1. Days 1–7: Select One Authorized Route and Protect the Pod
paragraphs: Start Day 1 by choosing one buyer problem, one software category, and one primary transaction route. A workable wedge is license rationalization followed by an authorized security-platform renewal for companies with 200–1,000 employees. Because the supplied metadata specifies nine plays without their individual names, use this explicit chapter-level working map: P1 authorized VAR resale; P2 registered-deal sourcing; P3 AWS Channel Partner Private Offers (CPPO); P4 Microsoft Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) transactions; P5 license reconciliation; P6 fixed-scope implementation; P7 migration and integration; P8 managed administration and support; and P9 renewal and expansion management. These are connected motions, not nine independent businesses or nine additive revenue pools. Tag each opportunity with one primary transaction play and applicable service plays, then count its billings once. Assign the two full-time seats to commercial ownership and solutions delivery. Use three contractors for channel operations, specialist engineering, and bookkeeping or contract administration within their competence. Reserve specialist counsel separately when needed. Publish named owners, hourly caps, and escalation coverage before approaching vendors. The sprint succeeds when this five-person pod can execute one narrow route repeatedly, not when it acquires a large collection of partner badges.

On Days 2–4, convert partner enthusiasm into documentary evidence. Request the reseller agreement, product and territory permissions, discount schedule, deal-registration rules, customer eligibility, support obligations, renewal ownership, and termination treatment. For AWS CPPO, distinguish the ISV's selling authorization from the reseller's customer-specific private offer; validate supported product, buyer account, payment schedule, and current AWS requirements. For Microsoft CSP, establish the actual direct-bill or indirect-reseller route, distributor relationship where applicable, customer relationship workflow, and relevant subscription cancellation rules. Neither a marketplace listing nor a distributor introduction proves authority to transact every product. Store source documents and retrieval dates in SharePoint or Google Drive, with permission-controlled links in HubSpot. For federal opportunities, examine FAR 12.212 and the solicitation's commercial-software terms before promising license rights. If contract information will enter reseller systems, check whether FAR 52.204-21 applies and implement its required safeguards. Exclude federal prospects from the launch wedge when the pod cannot support the solicitation's actual requirements. By Day 4, each route must be marked executable, pending a named document, or excluded, with no customer quote implying an authority the business has not obtained.

Set cash controls on Day 5 before paying for certifications or contractor availability. The canonical startup-capital range is $15,000–$75,000 and monthly operating expense range is $5,000–$25,000; this chapter selects a tighter $15,000 first-month operating-disbursement ceiling. Allocate at most $7,000 to full-time cash compensation, $3,000 to contractor work, $1,000 to operating tools, $1,500 to training and channel setup, and $2,500 to specialist review and contingency. These are budget limits, not assumed market salaries: existing compensation commitments must fit, or the launch needs more capital and a revised approved budget before starting. Keep at least $10,000 unrestricted cash outside this spending envelope, plus a separate reserve for unavoidable vendor payments, payroll liabilities, taxes, and potential customer refunds. Do not fund annual license purchases from the operating reserve. Use customer prepayment, matched distributor terms, or an independently funded order reserve before committing to vendor payables. On Days 6–7, build a sixty-account prospect list and test quote arithmetic without sending executable offers. Reject a launch budget that balances only by treating unpaid labor as free or assuming that an unsigned purchase order is available cash.
