sections.heading: 2. Days 8–14: Produce Buyer Evidence and Quote Real Contribution
paragraphs: Use Days 8–10 to discover buying mechanics rather than collect compliments about the product. Contact forty of the sixty researched accounts with individually relevant messages, and target eight completed discovery meetings by Day 14. A discovery meeting counts only when the buyer describes an operating problem and the seller records the incumbent product, renewal or project date, budget owner, procurement route, and next action. A qualified opportunity additionally requires an identified sponsor, plausible budget source, addressable scope, and a buyer-confirmed milestone within sixty days. Separate a buyer's willingness to discuss license waste from permission to upload license inventories. For P5, request an administrator-approved export containing only the fields needed for reconciliation; exclude credentials and unnecessary user attributes. Use P2 registration only after checking the vendor's eligibility and duplicate-deal rules. Record submitted, accepted, expired, and rejected registrations as different states. Commercial email must follow applicable CAN-SPAM requirements under 15 U.S.C. § 7704, including accurate routing information and working opt-out handling. The commercial lead owns suppression records. Do not claim a protected margin merely because a seller has entered a prospect into a partner portal.

On Days 11–12, build a quote waterfall that keeps customer billings, vendor costs, delivery costs, and net profit distinct. An illustrative Base economics block contains $100,000 in license resale and $40,000 in implementation billings, producing $140,000 gross revenue. Subtract $85,000 vendor cost and $20,000 direct delivery cost, leaving $35,000 contribution before allocated overhead. Subtract another $15,400 for selling, support, administration, transaction costs, collection-loss provision, and other modeled operating costs; owner net profit is $19,600, exactly 14%. Ten identical annual blocks reconcile to the canonical $1,400,000 Base revenue and $196,000 owner profit. This is an arithmetic bridge, not a prediction of ten first-year wins. The Conservative case requires total modeled costs of $276,000 against $300,000 billings; the Scaled case requires $2,000,000 costs against $2,500,000 billings. Do not insert a distributor rebate until its conditions and collection are supportable. Exclude sales tax collected for remittance from revenue. Reconcile the scorecard's gross-resale convention with the accountant's principal-versus-agent assessment for actual reporting; a referral-only transaction does not become gross license revenue simply because the underlying customer software purchase is large.

Days 13–14 turn the price sheet into a buyer-verifiable execution package. Issue no more than two fully scoped initial proposals per full-time seller during this week, leaving time for distributor confirmation and solution review. Each proposal identifies product SKU, quantity, subscription period, license contracting party, implementation exclusions, acceptance evidence, payment milestones, and quote expiry. Obtain a current vendor or distributor quote before promising a discount; show any marketplace charges as explicit assumptions until verified against applicable terms. Require projected contribution of at least 20% after vendor costs, direct delivery, and transaction charges for the initial blended package, then test whether allocated overhead still permits the 14% Base net target. A license-only quote below that contribution threshold belongs in Fix unless separately priced services create a documented viable package. Never condition basic license rights on an undisclosed service purchase. Build a payment calendar showing supplier due dates, customer acceptance, settlement dates, and cash exposure under a sixty-day delay. If the customer requires net-sixty terms while the distributor requires prepayment, change commercial terms or decline the order. A profitable invoice can still exhaust the pod's cash before the customer pays.

callout.body: Experienced channel operators preserve entitlement accuracy, registration protection, and settlement visibility before negotiating.
items: Keep the accepted registration identifier, expiry, vendor contact, and discount evidence beside the exact quote version.
For CPPO, confirm the selling authorization and buyer account before constructing the customer offer; test changed quantities against current permissions.

sections.heading: 3. Days 15–21: Rehearse Delivery, Settlement, and Renewal Automation
paragraphs: Week three tests whether the pod can deliver what the seller has described. On Day 15, the solutions lead and engineering contractor rehearse one P6 implementation in an authorized sandbox using synthetic records. Measure setup, integration, rollback, documentation, and handoff hours separately. On Day 16, rehearse P7 migration with a small representative dataset, agreed field mapping, validation totals, and a reversible cutover procedure. No production tenant changes occur merely because a prospect agreed to discovery. Under 18 U.S.C. § 1030, access boundaries matter; obtain explicit customer authorization defining accounts, systems, operations, and testing windows. If personal information is processed for a covered California business, examine the service-provider or contractor requirements in California Civil Code § 1798.100(d) and the applicable role definitions and implement the required contractual restrictions. Do not copy customer exports into general-purpose demonstration environments. The acceptance packet must show starting state, authorized changes, measured results, exceptions, and customer signoff criteria. Compare actual rehearsal hours with estimated hours, and flag variance above 20% for repricing before the next proposal. This prevents a high-margin license transaction from concealing an implementation obligation the small team cannot fulfill.

Days 17–18 establish support and renewal mechanics without creating an unlimited help desk. For P8, publish support hours, severity definitions, first-response targets, escalation destinations, and the distinction between reseller administration and vendor product support. Sell only the coverage the pod can staff; a three-contractor roster is not continuous staffed coverage. Use Jira Service Management or a similarly controlled ticket queue to record requests and acceptance issues. For P9, create renewal alerts at 120, 90, 60, and 30 days before the relevant contractual decision date, adjusted for vendor-specific notice periods. The commercial lead owns outreach; the channel contractor verifies current pricing and eligibility; the solutions lead checks quantities and adoption. Quote generation should populate approved SKUs, terms, currency, and price-expiry fields from controlled records rather than free-text guesses. License reconciliation should compare vendor entitlements with customer exports and flag discrepancies without automatically cancelling licenses. Test all three automation levers against ten synthetic cases, including expired registration, duplicate renewal, currency mismatch, missing account identifier, and changed seat count. Require all ten cases to route correctly, with zero duplicate outbound quotes and zero unauthorized changes, before enabling customer-facing automation.

On Days 19–21, rehearse the entire order-to-cash chain with a clearly labeled internal test order. Trace buyer approval, reseller offer, supplier order, entitlement delivery, service acceptance, customer invoice, marketplace or distributor statement, and bank receipt. A marketplace acceptance is not automatically the date funds become available; retrieve the applicable settlement terms and model actual disbursement timing. Assign the bookkeeping contractor a weekly reconciliation matching invoice identifiers, credits, fees, taxes, and deposits. Record disputed receivables separately from ordinary aging. Apply a 20% delivery-hour overrun, a two-percentage-point reduction in resale spread, and a sixty-day collection delay to every near-term proposal. These are separate stress assumptions, not edits to the canonical scorecard. An opportunity fails the cash test if any dated balance falls below the protected reserve after committed payments. By Day 21, produce a capacity board showing customer-facing work, quote review, support, and contractor hours for the next four weeks. Plan against eighty weekly full-time hours and no more than twenty aggregate contractor hours in the launch model, subject to actual rates and budget. Leave at least twenty percent of planned capacity unallocated for exceptions and customer delays.

sections.heading: 4. Days 22–30 and Beyond: Decide with Evidence, Cash, and Capacity
paragraphs: Days 22–29 consolidate evidence into a decision packet rather than manufacture urgency around month-end. Revisit every open opportunity with its sponsor, confirm the next dated procurement action, and remove opportunities whose only evidence is seller optimism. A procurement-validated opportunity has a buyer-confirmed purchasing route, documented approval participants, timing, and an accepted next action; it need not have a signed order. Track unweighted quoted gross billings separately from contribution and collected cash. For Day 30, require at least six qualified opportunities, two buyer-reviewed proposals, and $150,000 of unweighted proposed billings to permit a limited Scale decision. Also require written route authorization, passing quote and automation controls, at least 20% projected package contribution, a modeled 14% annual net margin at Base utilization, and protected cash after commitments. These thresholds are management rules for this sprint, not observed conversion benchmarks. Two proposals cannot establish a dependable win rate. Because the canonical first-deal interval is three to twelve months, zero closed revenue at Day 30 is expected in many valid launches. Scale here means concentrating existing effort on the validated route, not adding full-time seats or buying speculative annual license inventory.

Apply the decision matrix in precedence order: Kill overrides Fix, and Scale requires every stated condition. Kill the affected route immediately for explicit vendor refusal, fabricated selling authority, or a forecast breach of protected cash that cannot be cured before commitment. At Day 30, Kill the current segment when forty researched contacts and eight completed discovery meetings produce fewer than two qualified opportunities and no buyer-confirmed next milestone. Incomplete outreach is an execution failure requiring Fix, not proof that demand is absent. Fix receives one owner, one measurable correction, and a fourteen-day deadline; freeze incremental discretionary spending while the correction runs. At Day 60, require ten qualified opportunities, four buyer-reviewed proposals, and at least two procurement-validated opportunities for controlled expansion within the existing pod. At Day 90, require twelve qualified opportunities, six reviewed proposals, and either one executable order with funded supplier obligations or three procurement-validated opportunities with buyer-confirmed decisions inside ninety days. Do not confuse this pipeline milestone with achieved profitability. Pause or replace a route whose buyers repeatedly refuse the next concrete action, while retaining legitimate support and contractual obligations for any customers already served.

Cap cumulative operating disbursements at $15,000 through Day 30, $30,000 through Day 60, and $45,000 through Day 90, always subject to the tighter available-cash test. Additional spending capacity equals opening unrestricted cash plus collected operating receipts, less disbursements already made, the $10,000 reserve, and ring-fenced unavoidable obligations. Future receivables and unsigned funding promises contribute zero. A business starting with $25,000 therefore cannot automatically spend $30,000 by Day 60; without additional available cash it must pause sooner. Keep license-order funding separate, and prohibit a supplier commitment that consumes protected operating liquidity. On Day 30, publish the chosen route, each failed threshold, remediation owners, and the next review date. Maintain the 2 FT + 3 C pod through controlled validation; the canonical Scaled team of 3 FT + 4 C belongs to the $2,500,000 annual-revenue, $500,000 annual-profit operating case, not an automatic ninety-day hiring plan. Before increasing headcount, require signed backlog and recurring gross contribution sufficient to cover three months of incremental fully loaded labor while preserving reserves. Preserve the canonical annual profit cases as planning anchors, and report actual bookings, recognized revenue, receipts, and owner profit as separate measures.

chapters.pull_quote: Scale the route that survives authorization, delivery, and cash testing—not the pipeline that looks largest in a presentation.
action_checklist: Assign the P1–P9 working map to two full-time owners and three capped contractors, selecting one primary transaction route.
Collect reseller authority, registration rules, supplier pricing, subscription restrictions, and customer procurement requirements before executable quoting.
Build the $15,000 launch budget, protect at least $10,000 plus unavoidable obligations, and separately fund every license-order exposure.
Complete the daily discovery, quote, delivery, and automation deliverables, retaining buyer confirmations and ten passing synthetic control tests.
Reconcile every proposal to vendor costs, direct labor, transaction charges, overhead, and dated cash exposure without double-counting mapped plays.
Publish Day 30/60/90 Kill, Fix, or Scale decisions using the matrix, fourteen-day correction deadlines, and the tighter available-cash ceiling.
